■ Report from a reader of this site: This is the parking lot at Yoshino Park Campground. It's incredibly cheap here: 500 yen per tent and 500 yen per campervan. It's also available at night. When using the facilities, please register at the Yoshino District Revitalization Center across the street. There's also a bathing facility (small, but...) that you can use for 300 yen! Bathing facility: Available days: Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday. Hours: October-May: 3 PM - 7 PM. June-September: 2 PM - 9 PM. Usage fee: As a cleaning cooperation fee, 300 yen for adults, 200 yen for junior high school students and younger. (Note) Soap and towels are not provided, so please bring your own. ...However, rinse-in shampoo and body soap are provided courtesy of the center. Bringing your own towel is essential! The toilets do not have bidets, but they are relatively clean. Toilet paper is also provided. They can be used at night. There is also a cooking area next to the toilet entrance. Opening period: Late April (after snow melts) to late October (In 2025, check-out was from April 29th to October 31st). Usage time: Check-in 13:00 to check-out 10:00. How to use: No reservation required. If checking in on Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday, or Sunday: After arrival, please register at the facility across from the campsite (Yoshino District Revitalization Center). If you arrive before the Yoshino District Revitalization Center opens, please register after the center opens. (You can use the campsite even before registration if it is after 13:00.) ▼Opening hours of the Yoshino District Revitalization Center: April-May, October: from 15:00. June-September: from 14:00. If checking in on Monday, Thursday, or Friday, the facility manager will come to collect payment in the evening of that day or the morning of the following day. <Inquiries> Yoshino District Revitalization Center Tel: 0125-73-2632 (From Shintotsukawa HP) This is one of my favorite places that I always use at least once a season. You can use the bath and stay overnight for only ¥800, and if you avoid the high season, it's quiet and comfortable both day and night! Spring and autumn seasons are recommended. There is nothing around. Only the center and post office...no convenience stores, but there is a Coca-Cola vending machine at the entrance of the center. (Posted by Kita no Bug Tracker, April 2026)

■Manager's rating ★5!! (Spring quality 4.5, Scenery 0.5+α) Located at the back of Shikaribetsu Gorge Campground. Note that the bath is only cleaned during the Shikaribetsu Gorge Campground's opening period (July 1st - September 30th). If it's not cleaned, a large amount of algae will be attached and floating in the water. There is a path leading down to Shika-no-yu to the left of the cooking area. It's not a very difficult path. The water is a thick, cloudy moss green, and the bath is covered with brown deposits. It's similar to Yunotsu Onsen in Shimane. Spring quality gets a perfect 4.5. And the scenery here is also very wonderful. One of the best views in the country. A clear stream flows beside it, and you can see a panoramic view of a broadleaf forest. Autumn must be the best. 0.5 out of 5. A superb wild hot spring with a total rating of 5 out of 5. There are no words to describe how truly wonderful it is. There are tons of insects (blood-sucking gnats), so insect repellent is a must. You should apply insect repellent spray the moment you get out of the bath. Anyway, it's absolutely wonderful. A truly moving natural hot spring. The caretaker loves hot springs like this.

Regarding the parking lot, the entire area has a steep slope that goes down towards the sea. All the parking spaces are directly sideways to the slope, so it might be quite uncomfortable without spacers or something. The large space at the back seemed to have a slightly gentler slope, but tour buses and other vehicles start coming in early once it gets light, so I felt it wasn't suitable for getting a good night's sleep beyond a short nap to watch the sunrise. If you just want to sleep normally, I recommend the parking lot at Meiji Park, one of the few spots in Nemuro city. There's no slope and you can sleep peacefully. Because of these reasons, I ended up moving to Meiji Park before going to sleep this time. There are many open fields around Nemuro and not many open parking lots, so there aren't many spots for overnight stays in cars, but it's the closest base to Japan's easternmost point and a place where a fair number of travelers gather, so I hope it will be developed further in the future. I'll try to find one myself next time I go. (Posted: September 2020)

■Report from our site's readers: It's free to enter. It's thanks to the kindness of the locals. There are screens for privacy on all sides except the ocean, there's a roof, you can use soap, and there are washbasins. The changing area is next to the bath. Your valuables are safe, it's a hot spring at the very edge of the world that you can reach by car, and the sunset overlooking the Pacific Ocean is amazing. It's the northernmost and easternmost free hot spring in Japan, at the end of a road. It's a 3-minute walk from the parking area, and you can use your own soap. It's a natural hot spring with free-flowing water. Your valuables are safe as the changing area is right in front of you. It's separated for men and women. Women can bathe with peace of mind. Only the ocean side is open. You might be able to see the sunrise from Kunashir Island. I went in the evening. The locals clean it up, so be sure to say hello. There aren't any noisy people like at Kuma-no-yu, and it's very comfortable. There are few parking spaces, so I think it would be a nuisance to park overnight in your car. There were people camping at the fishing port further down the road, but bears have been sighted, so it's at your own risk, and there are power lines strung up. Is it really safe? I think a campsite or roadside station would be better. The nearby Sesoko Onsen was closed due to high tide, so we couldn't bathe there. The campsite is beyond the barrier, and cars cannot go beyond the barrier, but motorcyclists were able to park their bikes inside the campsite and camp. If you are staying overnight in your car, you will probably need to use the parking lot before the barrier, but during the day it seems to be the parking lot for the adjacent souvenir shop and restaurant, so you will need to ask the shop staff if you plan to use it during the day. When I visited (August 2025), the concrete toilet at the back was closed, but the log cabin-style toilet at the front was available. Also, the log cabin-style toilets at the front of the campsite were the only Western-style toilets with handicap facilities and bidet functions, but when I visited, a sign indicated they were out of order and the bidet was unusable. There are memorials and sacred sites for the Hokkaido Southwest Offshore Earthquake at the back of the campsite, but they are not visible from the campsite, so they are not a major concern. It is very quiet and the scenery is superb, but be aware that it can be windy as there is nothing to block the wind. Also, since this area suffered extensive damage from the Hokkaido Southwest Offshore Earthquake, caution is needed regarding tsunami disasters. (Posted: August 2025, by M)

While it is possible for the general public to use it for a short rest, including using the toilets, before getting on the highway, it is inappropriate for "overnight stays in a vehicle." *In fact, snow removal work will be carried out during this period (from November 2020 onwards), so if general vehicles remain in the station for a long time, it will interfere with the work. For the reasons above, I request that it be removed. I think this map is very useful, but showing parking lots that are not intended for their original purpose, as in this point, not only inconveniences unrelated people but could also lead to the perception that overnight stays in vehicles themselves are bad in the future. Therefore, I would like you to carefully review when adding points. (Submitted by: Mr. T, October 2020)

■Report from our site's reader: The toilets have been renovated and are very clean. They are not closed at night and are brightly lit with motion sensors. There is no charge for use. All are flush toilets with bidet functions. There is a convenience store behind the toilets, and Tanaka Ryokan is a hot spring resort for day trips. Please be aware of the operating hours of both. There is parking space for 5 cars in front of the toilets, but it is used by locals (mainly fishermen) in the middle of the night and early morning, so if you plan to park for a long time or stay overnight in your car, it is best to use the parking lot on the opposite side of the lighthouse park. If you park facing the lighthouse, the sun will rise from the rear. It is about 50m to the toilets. (They are considering prohibiting long-term parking in front of the toilets.) In terms of quietness, there is not much traffic, so it is quiet, but since it is across from Erimo Port, you will hear the sound of fishing boat engines around 11pm (departure) and around 5am (return). The elevation is 3.7m above sea level. Please check the evacuation route before going to bed. In the event of a Kuril Trench earthquake, it is estimated that a tsunami with a maximum height of 26m will arrive in about 30 minutes. Evacuation shelters are Erimo High School (elevation 43m) or the mountain behind the town hall. (Posted by naka0514k, June 2025)

There's a free parking lot on the west side with space for about 18 cars, so if you need to use the restroom at night, the west side parking lot might be convenient. However, this is primarily a parking lot for train passengers, so it's best to limit your use to the hot springs inside the station and then stay overnight in your car at "Michi-no-Eki Takahata" (Roadside Station Takahata). ■Report from our site's readers: Usage fee: Free. Flush toilets and cooking facilities are available 24 hours a day. The best campsite I know of. Of course, overnight stays in your car without a tent are permitted. However, it's closed during the winter, and only open from June to October. Cell phone (au) reception is unavailable. The nearest hot spring is Soma Onsen Ryokan, about 12km (approximately 30 minutes) away. Reservations seem to be the norm, but I've only ever checked in on the day (9am-5pm). I have been allowed to check in the next day when arriving at night. Another name for this campsite is "Parent-Child Interaction Auto Campground." When you think of auto campgrounds, you imagine cars and tents crammed together in a schoolyard-like area, but this place is a different world. There are 60 well-maintained grassy areas and parking spaces with ample spacing. It's also a good base for outdoor activities in the surrounding area, such as walks in Momoto Valley and climbing Mt. Moriyoshi. Aerial video is below (starting around 7 minutes) 👉️YouTube (Posted: April 2022, by Kusanoyu)

■Report from a reader of this site: Usage fee 500 yen (same price for overnight stays in a car or tent). Japanese-style toilet (flush toilet), coin shower (100 yen for 5 minutes), cooking area. ■Report from a reader of this site: There is a paved parking lot with space for about 30 cars and flush toilets that can be used even at night (I think the toilets were Western-style, but I can't remember). There are no views due to the surrounding trees. There are views of Hachinohe City from the nearby "Tsutsuji no Mori Campsite," which requires a fee and postal application. This is the trailhead for Mt. Hashikami, at an altitude of 610m. There is a nice shelter, "Hashikami-dake Daikaihei Rest Area," 80m away on foot (details), where toilets and water are also available. ■Report from a reader of this site: The toilet was usable even at night. There is only one streetlamp along the road, and the light switch is inside the toilet door, so it's best to park your car in front of the toilet. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Near the famous Meganebashi Bridge. A roadside station that seems to be renting space in a supermarket parking lot. Wasabi Ramen - 700 yen. The ramen comes with fresh wasabi that you grate yourself. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, May 2021)

■Report from our website reader: Free parking and restrooms available. Open 24 hours. It's very quiet and has a fairly large parking area. ■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking available. Flush toilets available. However, the main attraction, the "buried cypress forest," is not worth seeing. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking and restrooms available. Occasionally, police questioning occurs. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A considerable number of cars can be parked for free. It is a parking lot originally intended for travelers, with a 10-day parking limit, and there are notices for station and ancillary facility users. (There were no particular issues when using it only at night.) There is no closure at night. Clean toilets at the station are available during station hours (around 6am to 11pm). Outside of those hours, there is a 24-hour convenience store about a 2-minute walk away. There is also a police box next to it, so the area is safe. The area in front of the station is well-maintained, and there are chain restaurants and Aeon within walking distance, making it very convenient. Although it is next to the railway tracks, it is a Yamagata Shinkansen-only station with infrequent service, so it is quiet at night, and even during the day, only about one train per hour passes, so noise was not much of a concern. However, there are some public facilities, so there is some car traffic during the day, mainly from station users. There are no bathing facilities, but there are several day-trip bathing facilities in Higashine Onsen, about a 10-minute drive away. (Submitted by: Ikari, August 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: This is a recommended spot with a free campsite, a large parking lot, and restrooms. At the restaurant next to the parking lot (featured on the TV show "Life's Paradise"), a friendly couple serves food at reasonable prices until 8 PM. You can enjoy beautiful sunsets and starry skies at Misaki. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's readers: Free. Not only parking but also camping is free. Water is available at the cooking area. Toilets are 1-2 minutes from the parking lot. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Free. Toilets available. Seems quiet with no houses nearby. Visited in November 2023. However, we did not confirm whether the toilets are locked at night, so if they are unusable, it is possible to pull over to the nearby "Tadami River Rural Park" by car. It is likely that it will be closed during the winter due to heavy snow. (Submitted by: Kusanoyu, November 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free. No gates, etc. Elevation 1600m. Western-style flush toilets available at night, but no electric lighting. Water is only available in large plastic tanks for flushing (rainwater?) and handwashing. Great views, and you can see the sunset. Nothing to block strong winds. Gentle slope throughout the grounds. TV reception available. au has coverage, Rakuten Mobile has no coverage. Low traffic volume at night. Closed and inaccessible during snowy season. (Confirmed on-site in July 2024) (Submitted by: Kusanoyu, July 2024)

■Report from our site's readers: Free of charge. There are clean toilets, no houses nearby, and no passing vehicles, making it very quiet. Confirmed on-site in November 2023. There are multiple comments on Google Maps from people who have used it for overnight stays in their cars. It is likely that it will be closed during the winter due to heavy snowfall. (Posted by: Kusanoyu, November 2023)

■Report from our site's readers: Free of charge. Toilets are available for a fee (100 yen per use). The view is great, with night views of Tsuruoka city and fishing lights on the Sea of ​​Japan. (The day I stayed overnight in my car was the day of the Tsuruoka Fireworks Festival, and I had a great view from a high vantage point. There were several other people watching as well.) It's cool in the summer. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: Free. Toilets available (however, currently under renovation and unusable). Check out the Tsubunuma Campsite parking lot as well and use whichever is better. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: Free, no closures at night, toilets available, parking for about 30 regular cars, drinking fountain right next to the parking lot. A relatively new park that is long from east to west. There is a North Parking Lot at the northwest end and an East Parking Lot at the southeast end (details). The East Parking Lot also has toilets and is free to use 24 hours a day, but it only has space for 9 cars and is close to houses so it is not highly recommended. The North Parking Lot is across the road from a residential area, but the road is wide so it seems like it would be fine to leave the engine running at night. There are always 5 to 15 cars parked from morning to evening, and about 3 to 5 cars parked from night to early morning. There are also 1 or 2 cars that seem to be parked overnight. There is a convenience store a 5 minute drive away, and several supermarkets within 5 to 10 minutes (there are also 24-hour supermarkets). The toilets are Western style but there is no toilet paper, and the lights sometimes go out due to a sensor malfunction. Most users have local license plates, and taxis and construction workers also frequently use it for toilets and naps. It is fairly close to the center of Sendai and has good access to the surrounding area, so I think it is a hidden gem. (Posted by: T, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, open at night, toilets available, quiet. This is the free parking lot for Kappa-buchi and the Tono Monogatari Folklore Park. It's pitch black at night and so quiet that it's almost a little spooky, but that's what Tono is all about. Around 6am, a local woman was cleaning the toilets. (Submitted by: w, August 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available (may be closed in winter). Parking available for 31 regular cars. There's a small Tsurukame Ohashi observation deck within the parking lot. Located on a hill at the northern tip of the island, so it can be a bit windy. Traffic is light and there's nothing nearby, so it's quiet. There's also a parking lot with toilets for about 10 cars on the other side of the bridge (mainland side), but there are houses very close by. (Submitted by: t, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available (may be closed in winter). Parking for 37 regular cars is possible, including the nearby second parking lot. While some park toilets in Kesennuma City are closed in winter, all park toilets were usable until early January. Also, relatively newer, frequently used toilets have been fitted with anti-freezing measures and are usable. There are some slightly steep sections, but Ryumaizaki Lighthouse and walking trails are nearby. Traffic is very light, making it quite quiet. There are no convenience stores or supermarkets on this island. (Submitted by: t, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available (closed in winter). Parking for about 80 regular cars. Convenience store is 500m away, Aeon Mall is 1km away. It's a park with a baseball field and tennis courts, so it gets a little crowded on weekends with elementary and junior high school students being dropped off and picked up from practice. On weekdays, it's mainly used for resting, and after the evening, there are hardly any users. Overnight parking is sometimes seen. Trucks pass on the road next to it, but it's not too noisy. There are two toilets, but both are a little distance from the parking lot. (Submitted by: t, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available (usable in winter). Parking for 46 regular cars. A large park in the middle of a residential area, relatively quiet throughout the day. It is frequently used by local residents from morning to evening, and can be full on weekends. There are several supermarkets and convenience stores within a 5-minute drive. (Submitted by: t, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking for 58 regular cars. The toilets are Japanese style and not very clean. There is a convenience store within a 5-minute drive. There are green spaces to the north and west of the parking lot, and a sandy beach to the south. Swimming and BBQ are currently prohibited on the beach, but the fishing port next to the beach and the nearby breakwater are good fishing spots. The night view of the nearby thermal power plant and industrial complex is beautiful, but it gets very quiet and lonely at night. It is close to the open sea and there are no windbreaks, so it is very windy. Local young people sometimes gather there at night (especially in summer). (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's readers: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking for about 50 regular cars. Convenience store nearby, supermarket is a 5-minute drive away. A disaster prevention park attached to a large multi-purpose comprehensive park. There are a total of 5 parking lots, but only this disaster prevention park parking lot (Parking Lot 5) has toilets nearby. It opened in April 2023 and is very clean. It is not used often, with only occasional walks, and is quiet all day long, with almost no cars after sunset. Municipalities along the Sanriku coast have chimes on the disaster prevention administrative radio at set times, which also serve as equipment checks, but in Kesennuma City, the broadcast is at 6, 12, 18 and 21, and is quite loud, so don't be startled. *As of January 2024, Google Maps treats the BRT-only roads for the JR Kesennuma Line and Ofunato Line the same as regular roads, and may select them in navigation routes. This disaster prevention park may also be selected as a BRT-only road, or it may show an entrance for construction vehicles before it opens. It is recommended to check Street View and images from reviews beforehand. Details (Posted by: T, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking for 40 regular cars. There is an even larger space across the street where some people park. There are several convenience stores and supermarkets within a 3-10 minute drive. Families, dog walkers, and anglers come here. People play catch and play with remote-controlled cars on the adjacent grounds. All facilities are clean. After evening, there is almost no one there, and it becomes very quiet with no cars driving nearby. (Submitted by: t, January 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking available for 35 regular cars and 2 large trucks. Located next to Sendai Airport to the east, offering a good view of landings. It's about 2km to convenience stores and other commercial facilities. There are no houses or buildings nearby, and at night the traffic is so light it's eerily quiet. Aside from the occasional couple, there are hardly any users, so I don't feel safe from a security standpoint. There are no buildings other than the airport, so it's directly exposed to the wind. Since the earthquake, many other parks have been built on the east side of the Sendai Eastern Expressway and the Joban Expressway, but this is the only relatively large park that is free 24 hours a day, has toilets and parking, and is in a secluded location. From a security standpoint, it might be best to avoid using it at night. Also, the tsunami reached roughly as far as the Sendai Eastern Expressway during the earthquake, so there are concerns about that as well. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilet available. Parking for about 25 regular cars. Convenience stores and supermarkets are within a 5-minute drive. It is located near the Sanriku Expressway Kesennuma Chuo Interchange and at the southern edge of the city, so access to all directions is good. The Route 45 in front of it has heavy traffic and people are speeding, so be careful when entering and exiting. It is probably best to assume that you can only enter and exit going in the northbound (southbound) direction. It is frequently used by locals and can get full during the day. Large trucks also use it regularly, and combined with the traffic on Route 45, there is a fair amount of noise. Young people sometimes gather there on weekend nights. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking for 15 regular cars. Several convenience stores and supermarkets are within a 5-minute drive. Most users are dog walkers or jogging, so it's unlikely to be full. The toilets are a little far away but clean. It's within walking distance of the sightseeing boat dock and the fish market. At night, the area from the parking lot to the toilets is illuminated (not flashing), which is beautiful but might be a little unsettling for some. (Submitted by: t, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking for 100 regular cars. There is a trailer house cafe in the middle of the parking lot. It is a long park with well-maintained lawns and paved paths, and people come here to fish or walk their dogs. There are many families. Some people practice skateboarding. There are hardly any cars at night and no houses nearby. The only light is from the streetlights on the road. I think it is a very comfortable place if the weather is nice and it is not winter. There are convenience stores and supermarkets about 10 minutes away by car. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. There are two parking lots and toilets; the west side has space for several large buses and 37 regular cars, and the east side has space for 5 regular cars. The view is nice, and the sidewalks and lawns are well-maintained, so many people come to walk their dogs. It's located just a short distance up from the prefectural road, but not many tourists come here. A short walk further up is the Byakue Kannon Observatory, and the sunrise from here is incredibly beautiful. The downhill road opposite the prefectural road is a bit of a winding road, and some wannabe street racers from the area sometimes come here at night, but they're not the kind of people who will cause trouble. I recommend staying overnight in your car at the town-operated parking lot just below and coming here in the morning to watch the sunrise. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. A fairly large parking lot with space for 14 large buses and 310 regular cars. A convenience store is 5 minutes away, and a supermarket is 10 minutes away. It's a convenient location for sightseeing in Matsushima, being a 5-minute walk to Matsushima Kaigan Station. The uphill climb on the way back is tough, but using the Tamachi pedestrian overpass north of the station makes it a little easier, and it's interesting to go under and over the railway tracks. On holidays, it gets full of tourists by midday. There were several people sleeping in their cars. The station and police box are nearby, so the area is relatively safe, and the prefectural road in front has little traffic at night, making it quite good for sleeping in your car. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. There are toilets on the north and south sides of the parking area along the quay, and it can accommodate about 80 regular cars. The toilets are very clean. There are several convenience stores and supermarkets within a 5-minute drive. About half of the users are related to fishing boats, and there are also many taxi drivers and salespeople taking breaks. There are also many anglers, and you occasionally see campervans. Regardless of the time of day, there is a slight increase in car traffic when fishing boats depart, but I don't think it's a problem. (Submitted by: Mr. T, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available, parking for about 30 regular cars. It is located in an area with a fish market and related cold storage and logistics warehouses, and it seems that people who work nearby use it for commuting. Salespeople and taxi drivers also use it for breaks. Due to its location, there is a fair amount of truck traffic from late at night and early in the morning, so the area does not seem to be particularly unsafe. The toilets are on the breakwater between the beach and the beach, and below the breakwater there are fan-shaped steps. The parking lot gets crowded during the swimming season, which lasts for about a month. Outside of winter, surfers can also be seen there. There are water taps for washing feet and lawns, which are well maintained. There are several convenience stores within about 500m. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available, vending machines available. Parking available for over 60 regular cars. The entrance is difficult to find. Across the road are a home improvement store and a drug store. There are several convenience stores and supermarkets within 500m to 1km. It's a road that's like a shortcut to the national highway, so there's a fair amount of traffic. It gets quieter at night, but the speed is high so some noise is unavoidable. It doesn't feel like a park, but there are people fishing in the moat in front. There are 5 or 6 cars parked overnight. It's located between several residential areas, and police cars patrol, so the area doesn't seem unsafe. I think it's a pretty good place for overnight parking. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, no toilets. The Higashi-Matsushima municipal parking lot, right next to the Japan Air Self-Defense Force Matsushima Air Base, can accommodate about 100 cars. It's gravel, but well-maintained. There are no toilets, but there are some in a nearby park (open 8:30-18:00). There are several convenience stores and supermarkets within a 5-minute drive. The embankment near the parking lot is an excellent viewing spot, and you can see the Blue Impulse hangar up close. The aerial training is incredibly impressive. Training only takes place on weekdays, but the parking lot fills up from early morning. There's absolutely no shade, so be careful of the heat and wind. As a side note, about a third of the visitors are women, some coming alone and others with impressive cameras. The aerial training schedule is updated on Fridays → Details (Posted: January 2024, by t)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, roadside station-like facility, 24-hour usable flush toilets, not many people staying overnight in their cars, quiet, no windbreaks so cars can shake in strong winds. (Submitted by: Kusanoyu, March 2022)
■Report from our site's reader: The complete separation from the main line is great! Arrive early and secure a spot at the back of the regular car area. Recommended. (Older post from before 2019)

■Reader Report: Regarding Nogikawa Park on the Northern Tohoku Map, there was no toilet paper in the restroom. I was able to buy flushable tissues for 110 yen at a nearby Lawson convenience store. Also, I was stopped and questioned by a patrolling police car immediately after entering the parking lot. It seems the rumors about frequent patrols are true. (Submitted: October 2020, Anonymous)

■Reader Report: The parking lot behind a facility called Seishoen. The brightly lit mercury lamps turn off at night. The public restrooms don't have lights, so a light is essential at night. There's a strange noise from some kind of machine, which is eerie, but it's clean as it is regularly cleaned. I used it in the fall; it's highly likely it won't be usable in winter. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: I stayed overnight in my car on my way from Fukushima City to the Great East Japan Earthquake and Nuclear Disaster Memorial Museum. It's a commercial facility that serves as a reconstruction base, with a spacious parking lot and clean restrooms that are open 24 hours a day. There were no other passenger cars besides mine, but there were trucks parked overnight. Best of all, it's cool because of the high altitude (539m above sea level), so I think it's suitable for overnight stays in your car in the summer. PS There are a lot of creatures that are attracted to the lights. I saw a live diving beetle for the first time. It's a facility like a roadside station, so it's free. It's also open at night. It's very quiet because it's in the mountains. (Submitted by: w, August 2024)
■Report from our website reader: A chain restaurant originating in Fukushima Prefecture, famous for its crab pilaf. Tabelog, details (Posted: September 2024, by user n)
■Report from a reader of this site: Located along Fukushima Prefectural Road 65, near the Himawari Kotsu bus depot. Radiation testing completed.
■Report from a reader of this site: There are signs and banners indicating the way off Fukushima Prefectural Road 116.

■Report from our site's reader: The Takizakura large parking lot in Tamura-gun, Fukushima Prefecture, was chained off in the evening and inaccessible. (Submitted by: A, May 2025)

The cherry blossoms here are lit up until around 9:00 PM, so it gets crowded. If you plan to stay overnight in your car, it's best to arrive after 10:00 PM. You can stay overnight in your car and take photos in the early morning. (Many people stay overnight elsewhere and come here in the early morning because the toilets smell.) There is a 300 yen fee per person to view the cherry blossoms. If you want to see the illuminated cherry blossoms at night, you'll have to spend the whole day here after staying overnight in your car, or come in the afternoon and wait in traffic for several hours.

■Report from our website reader: It's newly built, so there's a large parking lot and clean toilets. There's also one restaurant that's open until late at night. Details (older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A free parking lot with space for about 60 regular cars. The toilets are simple flush toilets and are kept clean. You can spend a quiet night in this spacious parking lot. (The link on the overnight parking map is no longer used on the current company website, and it is highly likely that the old information has been left up.) (Submitted: November 2025, anonymous)

■Report from a reader of this site: The station building (camp shelter) is usually staffed by a caretaker during the day and closed at night, but the toilets are available 24 hours a day. During winter (mid-November onwards), it is inaccessible due to snow and the toilets are closed. Hot springs are located in the nearby village and at Appi Resort. It is a suitable base for enjoying the surrounding natural environment. There is some car traffic even in the early morning. Elevation 842m. Last on-site confirmation June 2021. (Submitted by: Kusanoyu, May 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: Asaka SA showers are now 24 hours. See attached image. Here are some thoughts. You enter the shower room, lock the door, and insert 200 yen to start. Only 100 yen coins are accepted. You can get change at the 24-hour shop. There is a changing space of about half a tatami mat at the entrance, and the shower room is also about half a tatami mat. The hot water runs for 10 minutes, and the rest of the time is free. There are buttons to turn the shower on and off and the remaining time is displayed. It resets when you unlock the shower room door. I left with 3 minutes left. But I think it's a great deal. There is a sink and hairdryer in front of the shower room, which is helpful. There are 3 shower rooms, and although there are several people in line both day and night, you can get in after a 5-10 minute wait. There is also one shower room for women. That's all for my report. (Posted: October 2022, Chiba Prefecture, Ms. S)
■Coin-operated showers available (24 hours, 300 yen/10 minutes).

■Report from our website reader: The facility is clean after the renovation. There is a wide variety of goods for sale. It is great that they have a place to dispose of combustible waste. There are also plenty of toilets. The parking lot is spacious and quiet because it is not on a main road. It is also good that large vehicles and regular vehicles are separated. (Submitted by: t, November 2023)
■Report from our website reader: Hotel Tappi offers bathing facilities, 24-hour toilets, and is quiet at night (older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: As others have written, the rest area itself is very small, but the area for regular cars is at the front. Large trucks park at the back, but because it's a small rest area, they park facing the direction of travel on the main road, so the idling noise is not easily heard. However, it's right next to the main road of the Tohoku Expressway, so if you don't mind, it's probably better than the idling noise of large trucks. If it bothers you, you might want to bring earplugs. There is always the idling noise of large trucks at rest areas on expressways, so I think it can't be helped. (Posted: June 2023, by a reader)

■Extremely narrow. The main road is right behind the regular car parking area, so it's extremely noisy. Getting a good night's sleep is impossible. You should avoid this place. However, the fact that there is a water refill is good. It is unclear whether it is famous spring water or just tap water. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's along a bypass, but it's a bit far away so it's not too bothersome. There are flush toilets. The compressor at the shop might be a little noisy! There are houses nearby, so loud noises are strictly prohibited. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking and public toilets. It's noisy because it's along a main road. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website readers: During the peak season in April, private vehicles cannot drive directly onto Hanamiyama. You must take a shuttle bus (fee required / approximately 10 minutes) to get to Hanamiyama.

■Report from a reader of this site: Toilets are not closed at night. Western-style flush toilets are clean. au signal is decent (2 bars). There is a fair amount of traffic, and although it's a little distance from the road, the traffic noise is noticeable. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Toilets are not closed at night. Western-style toilets are flushable and have toilet paper, and are clean. No cell phone reception issues. There is a sign prohibiting parking for non-park users. There is traffic noise because it is near a national highway. Earplugs are recommended. There are upper and lower levels, and the upper level is quieter. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Toilets are not closed at night. Western-style flush toilets with toilet paper are clean. No cell phone reception issues. It's small. There are no signs prohibiting parking for non-park users. It's closer to the national highway on the north side, so there is noise. It's a new park and clean. It's also designated as a tsunami evacuation site. There's a 17 Ice cream vending machine. When I went to investigate around 9 PM, there were people playing basketball in loud cars. There were other cars parked there as well, giving the impression that it's a hangout for residents. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Toilets are not closed at night. Located next to a residential area. One Western-style toilet and one Japanese-style toilet with flush toilet paper. There is a fair amount of traffic. No cell phone reception issues. There is a sign prohibiting parking for non-park users. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Toilets are not closed at night, and the Western-style flush toilets are clean. The area is flat and there are no problems with cell phone reception. There is a convenience store, supermarket, and home center next door, and there are streetlights, so the area is safe. There is some traffic. Earplugs are recommended. There is a hospital nearby, so concerns are about emergency vehicles and whether there are any people playing in the park at night. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Toilets are not closed at night, have automatic lighting and feel clean. Japanese-style toilets with flush toilet paper. The entire parking lot is sloped. Only 8 spaces are almost flat, so park there. au signal is decent (2 bars). Almost no traffic. Earplugs recommended as it's next to a road. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)
■Free parking, toilets available, cell phone reception OK (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: No toilet, all gravel, but it's flat which is good. It's noisy because it's along a national highway. It's small. Not worth staying overnight. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: A notice was posted stating that the toilets would be closed (the building still exists, but operations have been discontinued), so please remove them from the map. Confirmed March 2025 (Posted by: Kusanoyu, April 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: There were signs at the toilet entrances (multiple locations) saying "Please refrain from overnight parking..." Perhaps because of this, there were only about 5-6 cars parked overnight on Sunday. However, on the previous Saturday, there were dozens of cars parked overnight. Of course, the toilets (with bidet functions) were available for overnight use. Also, there was no reprimand for staying overnight in a car. Overnight stay in a car from August 2-4, 2025. (Submitted by MO from Chiba Prefecture, August 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: On September 19, 2019, I went to the Inawashiro Roadside Station in Fukushima Prefecture. The showers were marked "for emergency use during disasters" and off-limits. There were photos of two nearby hot springs, and I went to "Lakeside Banko." It was about an 8-minute drive one way. The price had increased from 600 yen to 800 yen. I had the open-air bath all to myself, and it was nice to be able to see Lake Inawashiro. (Older posts from before 2019)
■Report from a reader of this site: Used on July 15-16. Parked next to a space for 6 RVs in the RV park. The parking lot lights were turned off at 8 PM. It was relatively quiet, which was nice. The only drawback is that, although it's seasonal, small insects fly around. (Older posts from before 2019)
■At night, there is little traffic and it is relatively quiet, which is very good. The only noise is the idling of trucks. WiMAX is also available, which is very good. (Older posts from before 2019)
■[RV Park Michi-no-Eki Inawashiro] 1 night 2000 yen/1 vehicle, power included, details
■Opened in November 2016. The back area seems quiet and nice.

■Report from a reader of this site: The toilet was out of order and unusable. (Repair date unknown) It's along a national highway, but it's not a road where you can speed, so the traffic noise isn't too bad. Tourists arrived around 6 AM and woke me up. It's a good idea to wear earplugs. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)
■There is a flush toilet. There is also an observation deck overlooking Hotokegaura. (Older post from before 2019)
■There is a slight slope. The toilet is a flush Western-style toilet. Cell phone reception is weak. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: The toilet is inside the building and is closed at night. Is it available from 9 AM? It's unclear what time it opens at night. There is one EV charging spot. There appear to be second and third parking spaces along the road. There is no traffic at all. I successfully slept soundly without earplugs. I had two bars of au signal, which is pretty good. In some places, it's nice in the shade of trees in the morning. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: The toilets were unavailable. Therefore, it is probably unsuitable for registration. Last visually confirmed by the user: August 2022 (Posted by: Kusanoyu, August 2022)
■Report from a reader of this site: Toilets available, good view from the observation deck, large parking lot, no commercial facilities. Last visually confirmed by the user: April 2022 (Posted by: Kusanoyu, May 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: The toilets are made of wood, are new, and have no doors or other means to close them off, so they can be used 24 hours a day, year-round. There are separate men's, women's, and multi-purpose stalls with bidet toilets. There is parking for about a dozen cars, with a slight slope in the front and back directions. There are no private houses or commercial facilities in the surrounding area. It is 600m to Yonomori Station. It is about 4km to the center of Tomioka (shopping malls, etc.). The area was declassified as a specific reconstruction and revitalization base area (point/line base area) on November 30, 2023, so it is possible to enjoy cherry blossoms in Yonomori during the blooming season. Confirmed on site in April 2025 (Posted by: Kusanoyu, April 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: The toilets consist of three rooms: men's, women's, and a multi-purpose room, each equipped with a bidet. They are also available at night. There are several hot springs in the nearby town (Hot Yuda is 2.1km away, see details). There are no places to buy groceries nearby, but "Super Osen" is recommended at 4.5km away. The location on the shore of the dam lake offers beautiful scenery for walks: a submerged forest in spring, a large waterfall (accessible by passing behind the overflowing sediment dam) and an iris garden in summer, and vibrant autumn colors in fall. There is a baseball field next door and houses 300m away. It was during Golden Week, but there were no other overnight vehicles, so it was quiet. All 6 TV channels were received well. Cell phone reception (AU) was also good. Winter availability is unknown. (Used on site in May 2024) (Posted by: Kusanoyu, May 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: There are no toilets nearby, they are located some distance away. (This place) is away from the road, so noise is not a problem. Since it is next to a baseball field, it may get crowded on weekends. The further back you go, the more it is covered in sand. I was able to sleep without earplugs. (Submitted by: s, September 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: The toilets are still new and very clean. There are two toilets that are open 24 hours. We stayed overnight in our car during Golden Week, and there were only four cars including ours. (When we moved the next morning and looked at a nearby roadside station, it was almost full.) It might be a hidden gem 😁 It was quiet at night and we were able to rest well. However, there are no convenience stores or supermarkets nearby, so you need to prepare in advance. There is a store called Monma Shoten inside the roadside station, and we were able to confirm that they have cup noodles, juice and simple daily necessities. It is a little inconvenient because it is away from the main national highway, but the sea is beautiful and the view is good, so it was worth it. You can go down to the boat landing by stairs, so you might be able to do night fishing. By the way, there were fishermen during the day (Posted by: Hii-chan, May 2023)
■Grand opening on April 11, 2021. It is away from the main national highway and seems quiet and nice. A promising newcomer.

■Report from a reader of this site: "I used the toilet at Don Quijote," but there was a sign at the nearby Don Quijote that said, "The toilets will be closed at night." I have a feeling they were having trouble with the increase in people using the toilets while staying overnight in their cars. (Submitted by n, June 2024)
■Maximum 800 yen for 12 hours! Use the toilet at the nearby Don Quijote. It's a hidden gem. Eat some beef tongue, drink some alcohol, and sleep here.

■Report from a reader of this site: The toilets were clean, but around 11:30 PM, someone banged loudly on my window, shook my car, and woke me up before giving me a thorough police questioning. Apparently, this park is a key spot for police questioning. (Submitted by Muscle Okada, June 2022)
■Free parking and public toilets. I was surprised that the toilets were very clean, even though it's in such a remote location. It's super quiet at night. A real hidden gem. (Confirmed by administrator, September 2020)
■Reader report from this site: A parking lot with a toilet. It was completely destroyed by the earthquake and tsunami, but has been repaired. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: The toilets have lighting and running water. Cleaning is done twice a day. The view of the Sea of ​​Japan is good, and the setting sun was beautiful. There is a large parking lot. It is located right above the aquarium. Last confirmed stay by the person who wrote the review. August 2022 (Posted by: Kusanoyu, August 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: Three toilets with bidet functions. Wi-Fi reaches the parking lot. There is a vending machine for fishing bait. No toilets in the second parking lot. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, May 2021)
■Report from our site's readers: Quiet with a toilet (older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's readers: There are toilets. Be careful as the temperature drops at night due to the high altitude. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: There are toilets, and it's quiet. It's nice and quiet at night. All the noisy cars use the free Sanriku Expressway. But it's a cruising spot (*What is a cruising spot?). Someone came in a car (-_-;) (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Toilets available, elevation 872m, good views after a short walk, famous for azaleas in May and June, walking trail to Mt. Murone summit (894m) takes about 20 minutes round trip, nearby Boyohira Campsite (paid, auto campsites available), road closed due to snow in winter, last visual confirmation by the author, May 2019 (Submitted: May 2022, Kusanoyu)

■Report from our site's reader: Toilet, Washlet 2. On the other side of the road, it is said that ayu (sweetfish) swim upstream, but there is a weir right at the roadside station, and the sound of the water is very loud. The road has little traffic. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, May 2021)
■Opened April 21, 2015.

■Report from a reader of this site: Toilets: 1 with bidet, 1 Japanese-style toilet. Rest area closed. No Wi-Fi. I almost hit a squirrel 2km before the destination. It was the first time I'd ever seen a squirrel. I thought "oh no," but when I looked in the rearview mirror, I had turned back. There's a campsite on the mountain ahead for 500 yen per person. You can see the Kitakami Basin from a little way up from the campsite. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, May 2021)

■Report from a reader of this site: There weren't many options for overnight stays in a car in the Tsugaru region, but this place has a toilet and hardly any cars pass by, so I was able to sleep comfortably. (Submitted by: t, August 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: Because of its moderate altitude, it's quite comfortable unless it's the peak of summer. The adjacent national highway has been relegated to the old road due to the opening of the Shinkukai Tunnel, so nighttime traffic is sparse, allowing for a quiet night. The parking lot is generally sloped, which is a drawback, but a few spaces on the valley side are flat. (Submitted by: y, July 2023)
■Altitude: 740m
■Report from our website reader: The restaurant that originated clam ramen, located in Lake Jusanko, a famous clam producing area. Details on Tabelog (Posted by n, June 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: Upon checking this August, the toilets were closed from 4 PM to 9 AM. (Posted: September 2024, Kusanoyu)
■Report from a reader of this site: There is a toilet that can be used at night (no lighting), it is quiet with few visitors at night, last confirmed stay by the person themselves was around 2019, elevation 580m (Posted: May 2022, Kusanoyu)

■Report from our site's reader: This is a beautifully maintained park. It is free to use. There are multiple toilets, and they are kept very clean. The park was created by developing an area that was damaged by the tsunami. There are various sports facilities, and you can even surf. There is a nice bath nearby, "Watari Onsen Torinoumi," a natural hot spring by the sea. (Submitted by: Saitama Kotaro, February 2023)
■Report from our website reader: A restaurant in Iwate Prefecture serving "Ankake Katsudon," a dish of pork cutlet topped with a savory sauce. Details on Tabelog (Posted by: n, April 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's along Route 103, but it's quiet and nice because there's no traffic at night. Lake Towada at dawn is very mystical. (Older post from before 2019)
■Free parking, toilets available, cell phone reception OK. There are plenty of free parking lots with toilets around Lake Towada. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: au has almost no signal (even if the antenna briefly shows up, it's unusable when needed). The slope of the entire area is quite steep. (Posted by Kusanoyu, July 2024)

■Toilets available, cell phone service OK, cool even in summer at an altitude of 1390m! (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: au has almost no signal (even when the antenna briefly shows a signal, it's unusable when needed). (Submitted by: Kusanoyu, July 2024)

■Toilets available, cell phone reception is barely adequate (older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: 900 yen, details. It's located in Matsushima, a famous tourist spot, but it's quiet because it's on a side street. There's also parking available. (Submitted by: A, June 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: 770 yen, details. It seems to be a YuYou Park as well, and if you make a reservation by phone, you can park your car overnight in the second parking lot (※free, but YuYou Park membership registration is required). There seem to be no restrictions on check-in and check-out times. The downside is that the only nearby toilet is at a 7-Eleven on the opposite side of the road, about a 4-5 minute walk away. It is near Route 4, so there is some noise, but I think it is within an acceptable range.

■Report from our site's reader: A parking lot that can accommodate nearly 50 cars. It's located along a road, but traffic is light, so it's quiet. The streetlights are bright. There is no gate to the parking lot. The toilets were available 24 hours a day. It looked new, but it didn't seem to be cleaned very often. On that day, about three cars with loud mufflers gathered there, making a lot of noise. There is a railroad crossing about 200m to the south, and freight trains and the Senseki Line pass by, so it's noticeable if you have your windows open. There were quite a few cars parked overnight. (Submitted by: A, October 2025)
■Report from our site's reader: 50 yen! Non-hot spring, details (Submitted: June 2025, by a reader)

■Report from our website reader: 500 yen, details. This is a convenient hot spring. A notable feature is the cheap and delicious yakitori (grilled chicken skewer) shop "Torisuzu" (takeout only) located in the parking lot. Locals order before bathing. (Submitted by: m, September 2022)
■Report from our website's readers: 500 yen, details. A hot spring like a local public bath. Parking available.
■Report from a reader of this site: 500 yen. Note that the closing time is early. Details (Submitted: June 2025, by a reader)
■Report from our website reader: 480 yen, 6:00 AM - 1:00 AM. Cafeteria and rest area available inside the reception area. Details (Posted by: n, February 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 400 yen, details. Sauna available. To enter the sauna, you need to wrap a bath towel around your waist, which can be rented at the reception for 100 yen. The open-air bath uses free-flowing hot spring water, and the water flows out from between the rocks, making it a shame to waste it. There is a line of people waiting for their turn in the single-person open-air bath. The design is a little suggestive, I wonder if the women's bath is the same. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, May 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: 290 yen, details, parking is hard to find, behind the credit union. The hot spring feels like an annex to the building facing the rotary. I was enjoying the free-flowing hot spring water when my whole body turned bright red, so don't push yourself too hard, you can dilute it with tap water. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, May 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: There are 24-hour toilets. There is also a hot spring called Yamabiko-no-Yu just a short drive away. There is also a supermarket. The safety is a bit questionable, though. I have used it for overnight stays in my car a few times. (Submitted by: m, August 2021)
■Report from our website readers: 24-hour restrooms available. Consult with the ramen shop if you plan to drink alcohol. Parking is OK until after 5 AM.

■ Reader Report: Used on February 17-18, 2025. It's not closed during winter. It was a day of heavy snow, but thanks to snowplows clearing the road in the early morning, we were able to depart without any problems. (Posted by tossan, February 2025)

■ Reader Report: During the Hirosaki Cherry Blossom Festival, the Hirosaki Roadside Station gets crowded, so I used the Inakadate Roadside Station instead. There was ample parking space for about 180 regular cars. For shopping, I used Benny Mart Kuroishi (2.3km), and for hot springs, I used the Senior Citizens' Rest House near the Inakadate Village Office (2.8km, 150 yen). (Older post from before 2019)

■ It's noisy because it's along a main road. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: September 7, 2025 (On-site verification) The roadside station itself is quite ordinary. The lifelong learning center located behind it is quiet and pleasant, with no trucks entering. Also, the adjacent Furusato Park has two gazebos and a water tap, making it convenient to use. There is a Lawson convenience store 350m towards Gojome. There are no baths nearby. (Submitted by tossan, September 2025)

■Although it is located along a main road, it has a vast parking lot, and the back area is quiet and very nice (easier to see in the aerial photo 👉️ details). The far eastern side (details) is also quiet. It is an excellent spot for overnight stays in a car. (On-site verification by administrator, June 2022)
■Report from a reader of this site: As of September 7, 2024, there was a "Closed" sign near the entrance from the national highway. (Submitted by: Kusanoyu, September 2024)

■Report from our website reader: Stayed in October 2023. There is a large parking lot behind the building. However, the noise from the large fans near the facilities (toilets) was loud, so I parked in front of the facilities. There wasn't much traffic, so it was quiet except in the early morning and I slept well. The toilets are new and clean. There is a convenience store within walking distance. The nearest hot spring is Myōmezu Onsen, a 15-minute drive away. (Submitted by: h, October 2023)

■Report from our website reader: Stayed in October 2023. A roadside station next to Fukushima Airport. The parking lot is not very big, so I could hear the idling of a large vehicle, but there was only one, and even that stopped in the middle of the night, so I was able to sleep well. Also, I never heard the sound of airplanes taking off or landing. The rest area, which also serves as a dining room, was available even after closing time. There is a convenience store a 5 minute drive away, and Ayuri Onsen is a 15 minute drive away. The toilets were new and clean. The men's urinal here was an unusual toilet that did not use water or electricity, but decomposed by microorganisms. (Submitted by: h, October 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Stayed in October 2023. The new toilets on the opposite side of the facility were closed at night and during winter, and the old toilets were quite smelly. At night, street racers stopped by several times for toilet breaks, and there was a loud noise only then, but otherwise it was quiet. There is a convenience store and hot springs in Gake Onsen, a 10-minute drive away. (Submitted by: h, October 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: I hadn't marked this place because the parking lot is small, but I thought I'd stop by after seeing the road sign. To my surprise, there were toilets on both ends of the parking lot with bidet functions. I only noticed the slope after seeing this, as mentioned in previous reports. Even though it's a main road, it's in the mountains, and there are only a few cars in one night; most turn before reaching the roadside station. (Submitted by: Wataridori Manyuki, May 2021)

■Located along the main road from Fukushima City to Aizuwakamatsu, it has surprisingly heavy traffic. Even though it's in the mountains, large trucks are constantly driving by. Street racers with loud engines (lol) also come here. Furthermore, the parking lot is sloped overall. I wouldn't really recommend it. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: I used this place during Golden Week in 2022. The free parking lot is beautifully maintained. As a disaster memorial, the foundations of houses that were swept away by the tsunami remain, and the parking lot is for viewing them. There is also a memorial monument. It seems to have been recently renovated, as there are hardly any cars at night, making it a hidden gem. The toilets right next to the parking lot have LED lights on 24 hours a day and are very clean. I wondered if it was inappropriate to park overnight in my car, but there were people (probably locals) having BBQs along the coast, and there were two other cars parked there that seemed to be there for overnight stays. (Submitted by: M, July 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: I stayed overnight in my car in October 2020. I was stopped and questioned by the police in the middle of the night. They asked me all sorts of questions for about 30 minutes. There are probably a lot of burglaries and other crimes in the area. On the one hand, the police patrols give me a sense of security, but being woken up in the middle of the night is a bit much! I recommend refraining from staying overnight in your car. (Submitted by Mr. T, April 2021)
■Opened on August 12, 2017. It's in Iitate Village.

■Report from a reader of this site: Used in September 2019. After sightseeing in Matsushima, I soaked in the hot springs at Yumemi no Kuni and then stayed overnight in my car here. It was quiet despite being along a main road. There's a convenience store next door. There's a fast charger for EVs. There was a family with no manners who had set up a table next to their car in the parking lot and were eating. If there are people like this who violate manners, more and more places will have to ban overnight parking. Absolutely do not do that! Also, loud music was playing from the speakers at 6 AM! Terrible! (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: The facility itself is a roadside station, so there's no problem there, but the manners of the people who gather there are bad. You'll see and hear ugly things, so people who want to sleep peacefully should pass this place up. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Reopened in September 2019 as a roadside station + earthquake recovery memorial park! The spacious parking lot and luxurious restrooms made for a comfortable experience. In case of an earthquake and tsunami, be sure to check the evacuation routes. The adjacent Earthquake and Tsunami Memorial Museum (free admission) is one of the best facilities of its kind in Japan and well worth a visit. (Submitted by: Y, November 2020)
■Report from our site's readers: Opened in July 2019. A roadside station located in the middle of the city, for better or for worse. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used in October 2019. Stayed here the night before going to "Annotaki" first thing the next morning. It's surprisingly quiet despite being along a main road. However, digital terrestrial television reception is unavailable... There is a fast charger for EVs. The nearest convenience store seems to be over 20km away. (Older post from before 2019)

■The adjacent main road is like a highway, with everyone driving at incredibly high speeds, making it very noisy. Large trucks make an extremely loud roar. (Older post from before 2019)

■Trucks also park in the regular car area. The idling is endlessly loud. Not highly recommended. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used in October 2019. After bathing at "Kakunodate Onsen" in the center of Kakunodate, I drove for about 15 minutes and stayed overnight in my car here. It was surprisingly quiet despite being along a national highway, and I was able to rest well. I went to the Kakunodate Samurai District first thing the next morning. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Parking is available for 20-30 cars. The toilet is unisex and basic, but it is a Western-style flush toilet with a hand-washing faucet. It is also available at night. Cars come during the day when it is cherry blossom season, but it is deserted at night. People fishing sometimes come in the early morning. The area further inside is quiet. There are separate men's and women's toilets at Akatsuchi Plaza, where the steam locomotive is located, about 200m uphill. It is unknown whether they are available in winter. (Visited in April 2024) (Posted by: Kusanoyu, April 2024)

Evaluation: I recently visited the temple on a motorcycle tour and met the head priest, so I asked him many questions. He said that he himself toured all over Japan when he was younger (he said he toured Japan 5 times...), and he was very understanding of camping and sleeping in cars. Currently, he says he can't camp out on his motorcycle, but when he goes on business trips, he loads a roof tent and side tarp. He says no permit is needed for overnight stays in his vehicle.

Review: I went to the bathing facility that was recommended to me, bought dinner at a supermarket on the way back, and spent a relaxing time until morning. It was very quiet, with only the sound of cars on the Tomei Expressway in the distance. I heard an owl hooting. While I was grilling yakitori over a bonfire, I sensed something around me...a bear? I shone my light on it and it was full of raccoons. There were about 20 of them. They seemed used to people and came within about 3 meters of me. In the morning, I thanked the head priest and asked about the bears, and he said it was okay because the bears' habitat is much further north. He also laughed and said that it's bamboo shoot season now, so I could take as many as I wanted. Shizuoka has many main roads, but there aren't many places where you can camp in your car or wild camp, so places like this are very welcome. Until now, when I wild camped in western Shizuoka Prefecture, I used the Tenryu River riverbed, but it was so noisy. I think I'll go to Aburayama-ji Temple next time. However, there might be a lot of mosquitoes. (Posted by K in March 2025)
