■Report from our site's reader: This is a free parking lot. There is a toilet (Western style), but there is only one stall which is unisex. However, as of February 2024, the lights are not working and the lock on the stall is broken, possibly due to a malfunction, so we recommend using the convenience store located about a 10-minute walk away. There is no closure at night, and the view is nice as it is by the sea. It seems to be a fishing spot, as there are many anglers in the early morning. There are only a few flat spaces at the back. Idling is strictly prohibited as there are houses nearby. (Submitted by: Sumishin, February 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: There is free parking. However, as of February 2024, it is under construction and unavailable, but a nice public restroom has been built. There are no nighttime closures, and the view is good as it is by the sea. It is a surfing spot, so it is likely to be crowded in the summer. It is quite quiet during the off-season, but be prepared to get covered in seawater and sand. There are no streetlights, so safety is your own responsibility, and convenience stores are far away. However, there is a hot spring town within walking distance, a little further away, and there are many inns that offer day-use hot springs. (Submitted by: Sumishin, February 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free parking and public toilet (pit toilet). Regular cars and large motorcycles can park. Parking for large vehicles is difficult. This parking lot is very close to the "Shitodono Cave," where Minamoto no Yoritomo hid. (Submitted by Kogetaro, February 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking (150 spaces for regular cars) and restrooms. The parking lot is located next to the adjacent Tsukuba General Gymnasium. The restrooms are a bit far away, but the parking lot at the very back is comfortable. (Submitted by: y, May 2022)

■Report from our site's readers: Free parking. Toilets are a short walk away, but you can use the ones at Hinata-mi Park. Right next to the towering dam wall. High elevation (693m), so it's cool in summer. There's a free public bath in the nearby Shima Onsen hot spring town. Signs prohibiting overnight parking are posted everywhere in the center of the hot spring town. Example of overnight parking: Details (older posts from before 2019)
■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking, restrooms, and a prefectural police security camera on the other side of the road (older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Free parking and restrooms available. It's located in a quiet area hidden from the road. It was featured once on YouTube (Tatsuo and Umiko). (Submitted by c, July 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Free parking. I'm unsure about the availability of toilets at night, but when I stayed in Oarai for about a week previously, there were several mini-campers parked there for several days. There are restaurants nearby, and a large shopping mall during the day, so I don't think it's inconvenient. (Submitted by: k, March 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: There is free parking and temporary toilets across the road. You can get a great view of the maglev train. (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)
■Report from our website reader: Free parking and temporary toilets available during cherry blossom season. (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking and restrooms (※Availability at night is unknown) (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking and restrooms (※Availability at night is unknown). There are also parking lots on the west and south sides. (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking and restrooms (※Uncertain whether they are available at night). It's noisy because it's located along a national highway. (Submitted by a reader in May 2025)

■Report from our website reader: Free parking and restrooms. Parking lots are scattered throughout the area. The parking lot on the north side offers a panoramic view of the Kofu Basin and night views. (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking and restrooms. A panoramic view of the linear motor. Slightly sloped. (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: Free parking and restrooms. There's a Lawson convenience store right nearby. It's along a national highway, but it's at a slightly lower elevation, which reduces the noise somewhat. It's mostly flat with gravel. (Submitted by a reader in May 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: There is free parking. The toilets are located below on the opposite side of the road and are available 24 hours a day, but they seem to be donation-based and require payment. Parking is also possible on the lakeside below the road. It's a spot for astrophotography, and even on a weekday, there were more than 10 cars there. There are no convenience stores nearby, so be careful about what you eat. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Free parking. P2A, P2B, and P3 are free. For some reason, P1 is paid. P3 can accommodate large vehicles. The torii gate of Hakone Shrine is a landmark. There are toilets, but the lights don't turn on at night so you need a flashlight. There is a convenience store nearby. A little further on is Ryuguden Honkan, where you can enjoy a day trip to the hot springs. 1994 yen for adults. Addendum: The toilet lights were on late at night. I think it was probably a timer that was set way off. There were only a few cars on Friday night, but it was full early Saturday morning. They were probably hikers. (Old post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: A huge, free, level gravel parking lot and toilets. There are tourist information boards and parking lot signs, so it seems to be a public parking lot, but details are unknown. Akagi Onsen and other attractions are nearby, but the roads are rough. Elevation: 688m (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)

■Report from our website reader: This is a free park parking lot. There are toilets, streetlights, vending machines for drinks, drinking water, and water refills. It's a park frequented by families and the elderly. It's quiet. It has a safe atmosphere for overnight stays in a car. (Submitted by: s, August 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: Free of charge. Clean toilets available. It's a great place with a grassy area and a slide. Kujukuri Beach is also nearby. However, there are many surfers, and although I haven't stayed overnight in my car yet, during the day there are rows of surfers' vans lined up, with people drying their wetsuits, so I think there are many surfers who stay overnight in their cars or park there from early in the morning. (Submitted by kangoo Tony in May 2021)

■Report from our website reader: Free. Because it's on a mountaintop, there are only basic toilet facilities. On weekends, people come to see the night view until late at night, so the engine noise is a bit bothersome. (Submitted by L, March 2021)

■Report from our website reader: Toilets available, free parking. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Free. Partially unpaved. The entrance is difficult to find. It's a 1-2 minute walk to the park's toilets and a 2-3 minute walk to the convenience store. It's a little distance from the road, so you can hear the sounds of the road. There are also people fishing. (Submitted by ttfromjn in August 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, no nighttime closures, running water, and outdoor showers (cold water) available (on December 30th, it was too cold to shower, but they were usable). You can use the toilets attached to Shirahama Park, which are not closed at night. The parking lot has both concrete and gravel areas. It's quiet at night. When we stayed on December 30th, 2023, there were no other users. The downside is that while there is cell phone reception, it's a bit weak and feels slow. There are several plump and cute stray cats 🎵 (Posted by: Oyoyo, December 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free, public restrooms available (a bit old), and quiet. The upper level parking lot is flat, while the lower level parking lot has a slight slope. It's a relatively small parking lot. (There is also a municipal parking lot nearby with cleaner restrooms, but that parking lot is sloped.) (Submitted by: s, June 2023)
■Report from our site's reader: There are free, clean public restrooms. The parking lot is relatively small. The parking lot has a slight slope. (Submitted by: s, June 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Free, 24 hours, toilets available. Parking available for about 20 regular cars and 15 large trucks. There are 24-hour convenience stores about 500m from each lane. Located along National Route 6, there is a lot of truck traffic day and night, so it is noisy. There is also a lot of large truck traffic. Regular cars use it less often. There are few houses nearby, so engine noise is not a problem. In early December, all the cars had their engines running. (Submitted by: t, December 2023)
■Report from our site's reader: Free, running water and toilet available, and there's an Aeon shopping mall across the street, making it convenient for grocery shopping. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's reader: It's gone (Submitted by: n, August 2024)
■Report from a reader of this site: It's gone (apparently it was closed due to poor manners of people drawing water) (Submitted by: n, September 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: The noise from the trains on the main line is a bit loud. The shops and food court are open from 7:00 to 22:00 on the northbound side and from 7:00 to 21:00 on the southbound side. There is a 24-hour convenience store about a 7-minute walk from outside the rest area. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: The sound of trains running on the main line is a bit loud. The shops and food court are open from 7:00 to 22:00 on the northbound side and from 6:30 to 22:00 on the southbound side. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from a reader of this site: The sound of trains running on the main line is a bit loud. The shop and food court are open from 5:00 to 21:00. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A full-fledged public auto campsite. Reservations can be made online. While there is a fee starting from around 4000 yen, you can freely use facilities such as garbage disposal, showers, laundry, black/gray tank disposal, electricity, water, and outdoor cooking. It might be a good place to stop and reset during a long road trip. (See older posts from before 2019 for detailed pricing information.)

■Report from our website's readers: Details of the sake brewery located in Daigahara-juku, Hokuto City. You can draw sake during business hours, from 9:30 to 16:30. Parking is available at the site of Daigahara-juku on the east side.

■ Reader Report: The north side toilets have been renovated and are now clean and new. The huge observation deck is unusable due to its age. (Submitted: May 2025, Reader)
■ Reader Report: There are two toilets, one on the north and one on the south side of the parking lot. The one on the south side is relatively cleaner. You can get a panoramic view of Kashima Port from the park. (Submitted: May 2022, a)
■Report from a reader of this site: Near Toyoshiki Station. To the left of the main hall of a shrine in Nagareyama City. Low water level.
■Report from our website reader: Weekday adult ticket price 920 yen, details (Submitted by: Turner, May 2025)
■Report from our site's readers: Hiratsuka Fishing Port Restaurant A restaurant directly operated by the fisheries cooperative. A popular restaurant serving fresh fish dishes caught locally. Tabelog
■Report from our website reader: While it's a standard-sized car, there are 7 parking spaces available. A coin laundry is also available. 500 yen. Details

■Report from a reader of this site: A parking lot that can accommodate about 60 regular cars. The toilets are flush toilets and are in good condition. The downsides are that the parking lot is not very deep, and the adjacent Prefectural Road r14 is a fast road, so the sound of cars driving by is noticeable. It's not so noisy that you can't sleep, but it's not recommended for people who want to spend a quiet night. (Submitted by: y, March 2025)

■Report from our website reader: A parking lot that can accommodate about 60 regular cars. The toilets are flush toilets with bidet functions and are kept clean. The parking lot is deep, and the adjacent prefectural road has little traffic, so it is very quiet at night. The fact that it is located in a residential area and next to private houses is a slight drawback. (Submitted by: y, May 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking lot can accommodate 30-40 regular cars. Including the unpaved space next to it, it can accommodate about 100 cars. The toilets are flush toilets with bidet functions and are in good condition. As a public toilet, it's excellent. There are no electric lights, so a smartphone flashlight is essential when going to the toilet. It is also a trailhead for Mt. Kaikomagatake, one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains, so there are hikers who stay overnight in their cars in preparation for early morning climbs. There are no houses nearby, so the quietness at night is top-notch. The elevation is 788m according to our on-site survey. The distance from the roadside station "Hakushu" is 3.5km. (Submitted by: y, November 2024)

■Report from our website reader: The vast parking lot with space for 270 regular cars is fantastic. The toilets are flush toilets and are in good condition. I used it on the night of the spring equinox and had it all to myself for a peaceful night. It's right on the Pacific Ocean, so I wouldn't recommend it to people who don't like the sound of waves. If the next morning is a Sunday, there's a morning market at the nearby Ohara fishing port. Having the local specialty, octopus rice, for breakfast is a great idea. (Submitted by: y, March 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: A vast parking lot that can accommodate about 150 regular cars. The toilets are also kept clean, which is a good impression. There is a convenience store at the intersection at the park entrance, which is convenient. Large vehicles also stop there for breaks, but since the parking lot is large, it is not a problem if you park further away. Although it is structurally separated, the sound of traffic from the adjacent R51 can still be heard, which is a slight complaint. (Submitted by: y, November 2022)
■Report from our website readers: There is a drinking fountain (and footbath) of Izu Nagaoka Onsen on the northwest side of the property.

■Report from our website readers: Fuji Motosuko Resort (Fuji Shibazakura Festival) Details You can see one of the largest shibazakura (moss phlox) displays in the Tokyo metropolitan area from mid-April to late May. During the season, admission is 600 yen and parking is 500 yen. Open from 8:00 to 17:00. During the season (especially on holidays), nearby national highways become congested.
■Report from our website reader: A popular seafood restaurant at the foot of Mt. Fuji. Their cushion-sized tempura is a specialty. (Tabelog)
■Report from our website reader: A viewpoint overlooking Mt. Fuji and the highway. There is parking space for about 7 cars. The road leading there is too narrow for oncoming traffic to pass.
■Report from our site's reader: This restaurant is said to be the birthplace of Hamamatsu gyoza. They also have branches at Hamamatsu SA (outbound lane) and inside Hamamatsu Station. (Tabelog)

■Reader Report: This is the parking lot at Takizawa Campground in Hamamatsu City. There are clean flush toilets at the campground. If you plan to camp at Takizawa Campground, you are required to submit a usage notification to the Hamamatsu City Kita Ward Office. The campground is free of charge. You can enjoy playing in the clean, clear waters of the Miyakoda River. During summer vacation, many families come to play in the water. (Submitted by: l, December 2023)

■Report from our website's readers: Hamamatsu Act Tower Observation Corridor (Details) Admission fee: 500 yen (Parking: 100 yen for 20 minutes) 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM. The tallest skyscraper in Shizuoka Prefecture. It may be closed for private events such as weddings, so please check in advance.
■Report from our website's readers: It is located under the elevated section of the Shin-Tomei Expressway, west of Hamamatsu SA.

■Report from a reader of this site: It's very quiet. Although it's on a riverbank, there's a nursing home next door and many houses nearby, so it's not a place that would make you feel uneasy. (※Unknown whether it can be used at night) (Submitted by a reader in November 2023)
■Report from our site's readers: Hachibei Shokudo, details. The birthplace of "Arirang Ramen," a local ramen dish from Chiba Prefecture. Tabelog
■Report from our website readers: Details of Yatsushiro Furusato Park You can see the night view of the Kofu Basin from the burial mound plaza.
■Report from our website reader: A popular restaurant serving "Hachioji Ramen," a local ramen dish in Hachioji City. (Tabelog)
■Report from a reader of this site: North of Kannami Station, northeast of Kannami Buddha Village Museum. Water is coming out of a pipe by the side of the road.

■Report from our website's readers: "Natural water from the Southern Alps" in Hakushu
■Report from our website's readers: There are about two water-drawing locations in front of the roadside station building. The water is disinfected for drinking.

■Report from our website's readers: Hakushu-Ojira Water (Details) Located near the central zone parking lot of the Hakushu-Ojira Forest Famous Water Park "Beruga".

■Report from our website's readers: There are many places around here where you can drink famous spring water, but I'm not familiar with "Ojira Water".
■Report from a reader of this site: There is a pipe with water flowing through it next to the shop.

■Report from our site's readers: The shops and food court are open from 6:00 to 24:00 on the northbound side and from 5:00 to 23:00 on the southbound side. There is also a 24-hour gyudon (beef bowl) restaurant on the southbound side. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: The shops and food court are open from 8:00 to 20:00, and there is a 24-hour convenience store on the southbound side. The northbound side is relatively quiet if you stay away from the large vehicles. The southbound side is adjacent to the parking area for large vehicles and is a bit noisy. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's readers: Umenoya, details, Tabelog. The restaurant that originated "Takeoka Ramen," a local ramen from Chiba Prefecture.

■Report from a reader of this site: The grounds of Baishoin Temple (Arai Yakushi). Water flows from the dragon statue in front of the Daihiden Hall, but the water volume is low. There is a well and a tap next to the bell tower, from which water can also be drawn. The temple grounds can be accessed from a narrow path on the north side (there is a sign prohibiting long-term parking).

■Report from our site's reader: This roadside station is built on the site of a former junior high school and has a large grassy area. It's all flat. Due to the possibility of being disturbed by the idling noise of trucks in the large vehicle parking lot at the western end, the eastern end is recommended for regular cars. There is no place to draw "spring water" as the name suggests on the premises. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: The main branch of "Ramen Jiro," a ramen shop with a passionate following. Be aware that the noodle portion is more than double that of a normal ramen shop (you can request a smaller portion when asked by the staff). No dedicated parking lot. Tabelog
■Report from our website reader: A ramen shop specializing in ninja-style ramen (Enshu Black). Details on Tabelog (Posted by n, June 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: Bathing 11am-4pm, 220 yen, details. Although it is a facility for fishermen, it is also available to the general public (Submitted: May 2025, by a reader)
■Report from our website reader: Parking available for 3-4 regular cars in front of the entrance. 550 yen (Tokyo public bath price), details (Submitted by a reader in March 2024)

■Report from our site's readers: The park is open to the public from 0:00 to 24:00 on Sundays, so you can enter during those hours. Be careful as there are rough gravel paths and crevasses. If you arrive late at night, bring a very bright light and check your surroundings before sleeping in your car. Occasionally, vehicles carrying people taking pictures pass by. Until you know the way, it's best not to go down the narrow alleys. Watch out for deer.

■Report from our website readers: Details of Nippara Limestone Cave The largest limestone cave in the Kanto region is located in Tokyo. Admission fee: 700 yen, open from 8:00 to 17:00 (8:30 to 16:30 from December to March), closed during the New Year holidays.

■Report from our website reader: Day trip bathing available. 900 yen, details. If Michi-no-Eki Ryogami Onsen is closed on Tuesdays, come here. Plus, on Tuesdays, the price is discounted from 900 yen to 700 yen. The view of the valley from the open-air bath is great. (Submitted by a reader in June 2023)

■Report from our website reader: Day trip bathing 700 yen, details. 12:00-20:00. The hot spring water is free-flowing with sulfurous smell, as it is heated, diluted, and not recirculated due to the high temperature of the source. Meals are available at the [Gyoza no Manshu] restaurant inside the building. (Submitted by a reader in April 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: Day trip bathing 500 yen, closed Tuesdays, details (Submitted: June 2024, by a reader)

■Report from our website reader: A "day-trip shower" rather than a "hot spring." For those looking to save money on expensive hot springs around the Fuji Five Lakes area, or those who don't want to soak in a bath. 45 minutes for 500 yen (tax included), reception hours 6:00-21:00 (unavailable 10:00-15:00 for cleaning), towels and amenities included. Details (Posted by p in September 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Entering from Ninomiya, head towards Atsugi for about 2km. It's pretty good if there aren't any idling trucks. There's a 24-hour convenience store. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: A small park located at the foot of the Chikura Bridge in Minamiboso. Free admission, with clean restrooms. A spectacular view of the outer Boso Peninsula can be seen once you pass under the bridge. There are many anglers. (Submitted by kangoo Tony in May 2021)
■Report from our website reader: Nakaminato Yakisoba restaurant. Details, Tabelog (Posted: March 2025, by user n)

■Report from a reader of this site: There are separate men's and women's restrooms across the road (closed in winter). Cars pass by occasionally, but it is very quiet. There is a view of Lake Kawamata (older post from before 2019).

■Report from a reader of this site: There are separate men's and women's restrooms across the road. The cliff of the dam is right next to it. Perfect for dam enthusiasts. There are tourists all day long. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's quiet because it's away from the road, but occasionally cars driven by reckless drivers and police cars come in. There are vending machines and a toilet 200m away (older post from before 2019).

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a public restroom across the street (※Uncertain whether it is available at night). It is noisy as it is located along a main road. (Submitted by a reader in April 2025)

■ Reader Report: Also functions as a temporary parking lot when the roadside station is crowded. Only trucks are there, and it's noisy as it's along a main road. (Submitted by a reader in May 2025)

■ Reader Report: Although difficult to use after the earthquake, overnight parking is possible. There are toilets, but they haven't been refurbished since the earthquake. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: There were many noisy cars at Michi-no-Eki Yoshioka (including the large parking lot on the west side), so we took refuge there. Although it is adjacent to the roadside station, cars cannot go directly there and you have to take a detour, and the road is difficult to find, so be careful. It is quiet at night, and there are cars of people walking in the morning. (Submitted by a reader in March 2025)
■*Toilets are a walk away from the roadside station (far away). (2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: This is a free public parking lot with toilets similar to those at roadside rest areas (※Unknown whether it is available for use at night). (Submitted by a reader in July 2023)

Fuji climbing season (early July to early September), it becomes a parking lot and bus stop for climbers using the Subashiri trail to Mt. Fuji, and parking costs 1000 yen per car. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: After parking in the Todoroki Fudoson parking lot and walking down towards the gorge (crossing a river). The water quality is unknown, so use at your own risk.

■Near Chigo Daishido. There is a sign that says, "Please boil the water."
■Report from our website reader: The restaurant that originated Higashimatsuyama yakitori (pork). Tabelog, details (Posted: December 2025, by n)

■ Reader Report: Togane-Kujukuri Toll Road, shared lanes for both directions (turnaround possible), entrances and exits have at-grade intersections. Toilets, streetlights, vending machines, smoking area, public telephone available. (Submitted: August 2022, by s)

■ Reader Report: PA on the Togane-Kujukuri Toll Road. Only toilets and vending machines are installed. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Noisy due to being along the main highway. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Togane-Kujukuri Toll Road, southbound only. Toilets available, streetlights available, vending machines for drinks available, smoking area available, public telephone available. Daigata IC → Oshibori IC → Fukutawara Toll Gate → Fukutawara PA → Konumata IC → Imaizumi PA → Kujukuri IC → Makame JCT. When using this road, enter from Daigata IC or Oshibori IC. (Submitted by: s, August 2022)

■Report from our website reader: Naruse Gyoza, a specialty of Machida City, Tokyo, is a type of gyoza filling stuffed into a casing, similar to a sausage. For details, see Tabelog (Posted by n, August 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: One of Tokyo's three best stew restaurants. No parking available. Tabelog (restaurant review site)
■The basic menu is stew + draft beer + yakiton (grilled pork skewers). The beef offal stew is indeed exquisite and delicious, but the price is a bit high. There is a mandatory 300 yen cover charge. Also, since the yakiton here is grilled over charcoal, salt is recommended over sauce to enjoy the aroma of the charcoal.
■Report from our website reader: A restaurant specializing in fried chicken ramen. (Reviewed on Tabelog in June 2025 by user n)
■Report from a reader of this site: 800 yen on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays; discounts available on weekdays and after 4 PM. Details (Submitted by a reader in May 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: According to the staff, it's not drinking water, so please remove this post.

■Report from a reader of this site: Mizugatsuka Park. It's unclear if it's spring water, but there's a tap where you can get water next to "Mori no Eki Fujisan" (Forest Station Fujisan). A water refill spot before climbing Mt. Fuji.

■Report from a reader of this site: There are many anglers. Toilets are located across the road next to the baseball field (details). (*Unknown whether they are available at night) (Submitted by a reader in May 2025)

■ Reader Report: Evacuation locations and routes are designated in case of a tsunami, so it's a good idea to check them. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Reader Report: The southbound side faces the sea and offers good views. Shops and food courts are open from 8:00 to 19:00 on the northbound side and from 7:00 to 19:00 on the southbound side. Note that cars making loud noises often drive on the Seisho Bypass. (Older post from before 2019)

■Reader Report: I found a coin-operated car wash without a gate in Choshi. It seems perfect for washing the undercarriage of a campervan after returning from the beach. (Submitted by Sumishin, February 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: A huge free parking lot and toilets. Trucks are often seen taking naps there. The parking lot is divided into two sections, east and west, and you have to go out onto the public road to go between them. There is one toilet in each section. The first section has fewer cars than the second section where trucks park, and if you choose your spot carefully, it is quiet and you can get a good night's sleep. There is a hot spring next door (Shigemi no Yu, details). (Submitted by a reader in October 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Located on the grounds of "Jindai Nigiwai no Sato," a direct-sale market for agricultural products in Chofu City. 40 minutes of free parking. Details (Submitted by: n, August 2021)

■Report from our site's readers: Details of Inokura Sengen Meisui) Approximately 2km southwest from Orihara Station. The road gradually narrows, so be careful when passing other vehicles or making U-turns.

■Report from our site's readers: Parking fee 2500 yen (The parking fee posted was 2000 yen, but I think it has increased.) As already posted, the parking lot is temporarily closed after Disneyland closes. If you go to the Disneyland parking lot at night, the parking lot will not be open, so you will need to take a nap near the parking lot gate (the area in front of the parking lot gate is also blocked off). Once there are many cars taking naps, the parking lot gate will open and Disneyland parking staff will come to call you to guide you to move. (In my case, the guidance time for moving was 3:20 AM.) After that, you will need to take a nap in front of the parking lot gate until the parking lot opens. (In my case, the parking lot opened at 7:00 AM.) The parking ticket becomes a ticket for one free cup of coffee. Same hours as above. Toilets are at Yatsugatake Sanso and are tip-based (100 yen). The main entrance is closed, but the door on the left is open 24 hours and you can enter from there. During business hours, they offer delicious light meals such as curry, motsuni (offal stew), and fried bread, as well as alcohol, and there are vending machines for canned beer and juice. All of the above prices are a bit on the high side (mountain rates). There are no convenience stores nearby. It gets crowded with hikers sleeping in their cars on weekends from spring to autumn. It's below freezing in winter, but there are still customers. Snow tires are a must. If you don't take precautions, a 2L bottle of water will freeze completely. There is a good restaurant next door. Details: Steaks, pasta, coffee, alcohol, etc. Open until 8 pm. Bathing is available until 8 pm, 770 yen. Bathing is half price for those who have eaten there. Jujo Subway Station is a 4-minute walk (350m) west, and Tobakaido Station on the Keihan Main Line is a 9-minute walk (700m) east. The parking lot is mostly flat and can accommodate about 60 cars, but there weren't that many cars parked there considering it was Saturday night.
