It also became quiet around 10pm, presumably when operations ended. There is a huge shopping mall within 1km, which is convenient for shopping and you can eat at the food court. A negative point is that it is located in a potentially dangerous area in the event of a tsunami from a Nankai Trough earthquake. (Submitted by: y, May 2025)

■Report from our website reader: Free parking for 15 regular cars. The toilets are flush toilets with bidet functions and are in good condition. As a public toilet, it's absolutely perfect. There are few cars passing by at night, so you can spend a peaceful night. (Submitted by: y, October 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: A free parking lot located after crossing the Kanbara Pass on the way from Hida-Furukawa to Kamioka. (This is a new location.) There is a toilet. You can sleep peacefully here. However, there is nothing around, so it is suitable for people who like secluded places. (Old post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: For bathing, the Sabae City Community Exchange Center Shimin Hall Tsutsuji (details) is nearby. It's recommended because you can bathe and rest, and you can also use the gym if you bring your indoor shoes. (Open 10:00-22:00, 420 yen for adults, closed Thursdays and during the New Year holidays) Details (Posted: February 2024, by yuko)
■Report from a reader of this site: Initially, I planned to stay overnight in my car at the Michi-no-Eki Nishiyama Park, but there were many cars parked there at the beginning of the night (around 20:00), and there was a lot of traffic, so I gave up on staying overnight at the Michi-no-Eki and moved to the Sabae City Koyo Kaikan parking lot (details) next to the Michi-no-Eki. Parking fee: Free for up to 2 hours, 300 yen for up to 22 hours thereafter. Toilets: The toilets at the Michi-no-Eki have flush toilets with bidets, but the multipurpose toilet is closed at night. The Sabae City Koyo Kaikan parking lot is accessible from the roadside station (toilets) in about 1 minute and 30 seconds on foot (less than 100m). The roadside station parking lot has fewer spaces available late at night, but it gets crowded in the early morning (6:00), so it is not recommended for overnight stays in a car. The Sabae City Koyo Kaikan parking lot had space for only a few cars (3 or 4). There were no cars parked overnight. Other: There is a supermarket nearby, "Yasusaki Wai Plaza Gourmet Hall Sabae Store," about a 5-minute walk away, open from 9:00 to 21:00. (Posted by: n, October 2023)

■Report from our website reader: A 1-2 minute walk from the Puratto Park at Amigozakisaki SA (downbound). Restrooms available. Only regular cars can park in the Puratto Park parking lot, so this is more convenient for campervans, etc. Shop and take a break at the SA. (March 2022) (Submitted by: h, March 2022)

■Report from our website reader: Southbound only. After using this stop, you must pass through the toll booth further ahead. There are toilets and vending machines. The parking space is reasonably large. It is close to the main road, but the traffic volume is not that high. (Submitted by c, June 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: I stayed overnight in my car at the Ine Funaya Roadside Station. It was a weekday, so there were hardly any other people staying overnight in their cars. Be aware that there are no places to eat nearby once the roadside station closes. It's located on a hill, so you can enjoy a panoramic view of the town of Ine and the sea, so the view was fantastic. You can explore the town of Ine by going down the stairs, and you can also take a sightseeing boat and feed the seagulls. The toilets are average, but they are located in a secluded area, so I felt a little uneasy as a woman traveling alone. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking lot around the roadside station building is a bit cramped. The second parking lot on the north side across the road is recommended, although the toilets are further away. The adjacent National Route 176 has relatively little traffic at night, so you can enjoy a fairly quiet night. *Used in May 2024 (Posted by: y, June 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: A roadside station in name only, it's just a roadside station for stamp rallies. There's a large parking lot, but it's for another facility. The free parking is in an empty lot in front of the roadside station, there are no white lines and only a few cars can park there. A waste of time to stop by. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, June 2021)
■Report from our site's reader: It looks like a roadside rest area, but it's not. It closes at night, so overnight parking is not possible. (Submitted by c, June 2024)

■Reader Report from this Site: Additional Information about Michi-no-Eki Orihime-no-Sato: Currently, the soba noodle restaurant in the food court is temporarily closed, and only two restaurants (Japanese and Western) are open. Orihime Market, which also sells prepared foods, is open until 6:30 PM. They sell not only cooking ingredients but also seasonings, so it's reassuring. (Posted: November 2022, by yuko)

■Reader Report from this Site: Although located along the road, it's quiet and away from large vehicles. There's also a dog run, available 24 hours a day (though the website has time restrictions). Across the road are a large supermarket, gas station, and McDonald's. The toilets are newly built and clean. I went to the food court at the roadside station during opening hours, but for some reason, some shops were closed. It's recommended to contact them in advance if you plan to use their services. (Older post from before 2019)

■Opened April 17, 2014!

■Report from a reader of this site: The parking lot of this facility doesn't seem to be closed at night, and it has a men's restroom and a multi-purpose Western-style flush toilet. The name suggests it's a fishing spot, so it might get crowded during fishing season, but I don't know. (Submitted by yuko in February 2023)

■Report from our website reader: You can stay overnight in your car in the parking lot of Yutani Onsen. There are clean flush toilets. There is also running water. There is a footbath of Yutani Onsen on the east side of the parking lot. The baths of Horai Yu-Yu Arena are very close by. (Submitted by: l, December 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking for hikers with space for about 20 cars. Clean toilets available 24 hours, and there is a rest area. No vending machines, and no convenience stores nearby. It's quiet, but on a holiday morning in November, hikers start moving around 4am, and the parking lot is full by 6am. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: I stayed overnight in my car at Tenkawa Higashi Park. There is space to park about three cars. It is right next to the Shinkansen (bullet train) tracks. There are vending machines, clean 24-hour toilets, and a convenience store nearby. In the evenings, local people play in the park. (Submitted by: n, September 2024)
■Report from our site's readers: Details of the tea plantation in the sky The scenery of the tea plantation surrounded by mountains has become a hot topic online, being called "Gifu's Machu Picchu."

■Report from our site's reader: This is a free 24-hour parking lot in a park with a stunning view of Amanohashidate. It's spacious and flat. There are toilets in the parking lot, located at the park management office next to it, but they are closed at night. Toilets located within the park grounds, a short distance from the parking lot, appear to be open 24 hours. There is a bathing facility a 2-3 minute drive away (Kurhaus Iwataki, details) (Submitted by: Sunagon, November 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: You can fish and camp in your car, and there are toilets. There is also a bathing facility called "Sunrise Awaji" nearby. Marunaka Supermarket and Aeon are also close by. The downside is that anglers come and go in the middle of the night, so the noise might be a bit bothersome. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: It's usually free. During cherry blossom season, there's a 500 yen parking fee. It's located in the heart of the mountains, where the houses end. The toilets are old but clean; I didn't check the toilets for men, sorry. According to someone who participated in the early morning clean-up operation, trucks and other vehicles also come, so you might encounter some noise if you're unlucky. When I went on a weekday night, there were about 5 cars, but they might not have been cars parked overnight. Toryunada is nearby. (Posted: September 2025, by Catero, YouTube channel)

■Report from a reader of this site: A roadside station adjacent to the town hall. It's convenient because there's a supermarket and restaurants nearby. On the other hand, it might be a little noisy. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There is a town-operated paved parking lot and toilets (flush toilets, Western style, separate for men and women, and accessible for people with disabilities). Littering is not allowed. Many anglers use this parking lot to access the long breakwater in front of it. It would be an excellent spot for fishing enthusiasts. However, anglers may be coming and going early in the morning. Also, across from this is a large gravel parking lot, which is suitable for those who want to spend time in peace and quiet. It is private property but can be used freely and free of charge, and even large campervans are allowed. The owner is "Seramaru Aquaculture (090-1583-6773)". The sign says "Campervans are free for two days", but the owner said it is fine for any number of days. (Submitted by tossan in October 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: This sports park is on the outskirts of town, and the road is on the other side of the river, so it's quiet. There are few houses nearby, and it's a rural area. The parking lot is large and empty. The toilet is a Japanese style. The sensor light does turn on, but it flickers and seems to be on its way out. There are two vending machines. There are no roadside rest areas around here, so I searched for toilets and found this one. I came in the middle of the night on June 9, 2025, took a break, and left before it got light, so I don't know what it's like in the early morning. People might come to play sports early in the morning. (Submitted by: Catero, June 2025)

■Report from our site's readers: Parking fees are 100 yen/30 minutes from 7:00 to 22:00, 50 yen/30 minutes from 22:00 to 7:00, with a maximum of 1500 yen (per 24 hours). There are two parking lots: a bus parking lot (passenger cars allowed) along National Route 1, and a passenger car parking lot accessible from the east. Both have restrooms, which are generally clean. The bus parking lot faces National Route 1, so traffic noise might be a bit noticeable. (It wasn't noticeable with a multi-shade installed on a Hiace.) It's about a 10-minute walk to Meitetsu Higashi-Okazaki Station, making it convenient for dining out. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Parking is now charged. Details (Posted: May 2025, by p)
■Report from our website reader: Open 24 hours. The restrooms are clean, suggesting it's a relatively new store.

■Report from a reader of this site: The parking lot is slightly spacious. Facilities include two vending machines and a toilet. The trash cans are only for cans and plastic bottles (this seems to be a common pattern for trash cans at rest areas on the Maizuru-Wakasa Expressway to deter wild birds) (Submitted by: C, May 2024)
■Report from our website reader: The parking lot is spacious, surrounded by pine trees, and divided into several sections. The restrooms are also clean. (Submitted by: M, September 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking lot is small, but since the facility is inaccessible at night, there are no anglers. In the morning, it's bustling with people fishing. The toilets aren't very clean. If you're planning to sleep in your car, the parking lot one level higher is quieter and recommended. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: There is parking for about 10 cars. The toilets are Western-style and well-maintained. There is a grassy area in front and an observation deck with a great view. (Submitted by: m, September 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: The parking lot is divided into central and south sections, with the central section being for passenger cars only, making it quiet. During warmer months like summer, there are a lot of insects attracted to the lights, so be careful if you open your windows. Toilets are located outside the central store and at the northeast disaster prevention base where the helipad is located, and are available 24 hours a day. They are flush toilets (Western and Japanese style, only confirmed in the women's toilet). Truck parking spaces are on the south side. (Submitted by: s, October 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking lot is narrow and difficult to park in. There is a sign at the facility across the street saying "No entry for non-users" (Submitted by: Kousagi, May 2025)
■The roadside station's parking lot is sloped and noisy at night due to the coming and going of people, including express buses. Across the road from the roadside station is the Anamizu Town Library's parking lot (location here), which is quiet and very good, so we recommend it. We confirmed that it is not closed at night. (Administrator's on-site confirmation, November 2020)
■Opened in December 2015. Integrated with the train station. Since it is a terminal station, it seems unlikely that freight trains will be noisy at night.

■Report from a reader of this site: The parking area has space for 5 regular cars in 2 rows and 7 large vehicles in 1 row. The traffic on the main road is not heavy, but it is quite noisy due to the close proximity to the large vehicles. The only facilities are one vending machine and a toilet. It's a bit of a pain that the trash cans only accept cans and plastic bottles (apparently this is a common pattern for trash cans at rest areas on the Maizuru-Wakasa Expressway to deter wild birds) (Submitted by C in May 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: It was relatively quiet even during the day, and even if there was some traffic noise, I was able to sleep soundly with noise-canceling headphones on. Also, all the Western-style toilets had bidet functions (both men's and women's; multi-purpose toilets were not checked). (Submitted by yuko, February 2024)
■Free parking and public toilets. Confirmed that they are not closed at night. The toilets are clean, flush toilets, and include Western-style toilets (details). It is very quiet at night. (Administrator's on-site verification, December 2021)

■Report from a reader of this site: A children's park in front of the main gate of a junior high school. The toilets are new and clean. It appears to be well-maintained, perhaps because it is close to the school. There are only about six parking spaces. I used it during summer vacation, but if you park there during school hours, you might be reported as a suspicious vehicle. (Submitted by TOM, October 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: Himeji's soul food, a combination of Chinese noodles and Japanese-style broth. See Tabelog for details. Parking at Himeji Station South Exit (private car parking area) is free for 20 minutes. (Submitted by: n, October 2025)
■Restaurants where you can eat "Maneki no Ekisoba"

■Report from our website's readers: A base parking lot for sightseeing at Takeda Castle. Most people who climb Takeda Castle to see the sea of ​​clouds in the early morning stay here the night before. It's quiet because it's away from the main road. There are toilets available 24 hours a day, and the parking lot is never closed. Public Wi-Fi service from Asago City is available in the parking lot (older post from before 2019)
■Free parking, toilets available, mobile phone OK (older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: I'm a local so I've never stayed there, but this is the parking lot of Santepark Tahara. It's such a great facility that it's surprising it's not a "roadside station," with a direct sales market and a restaurant. The toilets are located under the bridge that connects the parking lot to the facility. It's near an old freight train. There are no bathing facilities or convenience stores nearby, but it's quiet. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: Parking lot 1 is paid from July 20th to August 14th, but free at all other times. There are toilets. Parking lot 2 is free all year round. The two are adjacent to each other. Hot showers are 100 yen for 3 minutes from July 20th to August 14th, and it may be noisy with swimmers in the summer. It is quiet at other times. The sunset is beautiful. Sea fishing is possible (mid-April to early January). (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A vast parking lot with a total of 1200 spaces from Parking Lot 1 to Parking Lot 12. However, it seems that the parking lots with higher numbers are closed at night. Toilets are located at key points, and Western-style toilets are available and are in good condition, but in some parking lots, the toilets are far away. The poster used Parking Lot 1 and had a comfortable night. (Posted by: y, October 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Oshima Kitano River Park → When I visited recently, the toilets were boarded up because they are unusable during the winter (December-March?). There are no alternative toilets nearby (there's a FamilyMart about a 5-minute drive away, but that's about it), so a vehicle with a toilet is recommended during the winter. (Submitted by: yuko, February 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Price: Free, Toilets: Available. It's quite quiet, even during the day, as if only a few people know about it. Originally, there are separate men's and women's toilets (Japanese style) + a multi-purpose Western-style flush toilet, but for some reason the multi-purpose toilet was unusable. I visited during the day, but it's so unpopular that it seems suitable for overnight stays in a car. (Submitted by: yuko, April 2022)

■Report from our website reader: Adults 300 yen (including sauna), children 100 yen. No amenities provided (hair dryer available in the changing room). Details: It's a town-run public bath, but it contains hot spring water, and is open to non-residents as well. I think it might be the cheapest in Ishikawa Prefecture. (Posted by: Ma, December 2023)

■ Reader Report: Large parking lot, toilets and parking available 24 hours. Toilets are Western-style with bidet and toilet paper. Large vehicles can park. There is a "Hikari no Yu" hot spring facility about 15 minutes away by car. There is a 24-hour Lawson convenience store next to the parking lot. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Reader Report: 24-hour toilets and Lawson convenience store, seafood restaurant open until 8 PM. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Several large trucks were also staying there. It was quiet, and they kindly allowed me to use the toilet in the middle of the night. (Submitted by: Doraemon, June 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's a large park. It's not closed at night, and the toilets are clean and Western-style. The downside is that there's nothing nearby, but on the other hand, it's quiet and you can sleep well. (Submitted by: Sumishin, May 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a multipurpose restroom. It is dark, quiet, and cool. There seems to be a restaurant and a shop, but I haven't tried them. (Posted by Takora in August 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Although a national highway runs nearby, there are no cars even during the day, so you can relax. There is plenty of parking even during long holidays. However, there are no shops nearby, so you should do your shopping along Route 42 before coming. (Older post from before 2019)
■Grand opening on April 7, 2018.

■Report from our site's reader: There is a slope throughout the area; most of the facilities have reopened; it will be crowded during the season, so please be considerate of others (Submitted by: Kousagi, May 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: I'm submitting information about the following rest area that I used recently. Meishin Expressway, Katsuragawa PA (downbound): There seems to be a severe shortage of space for large vehicles, and many of the spaces for small vehicles are occupied by trucks. You might end up near a truck no matter where you park, but if you have good earplugs, the engine noise shouldn't be a problem. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: I was able to spend my time in peace and quiet. There was some car noise, but I didn't find it too loud. I didn't find the slope to be a problem. The toilet was relatively clean, but the toilet seat was cold. There was a convenience store very close by, so it wasn't inconvenient. (Submitted by: Doraemon, June 2025)
■Report from our website reader: A restaurant serving Seto City's soul food, "Seto Yakisoba." Details on Tabelog (Posted by n, August 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: The west parking lot at Shinmei Park is now closed and no longer exists due to the construction of a retention pond. Confirmed on site. The north parking lot at Shinmei Park closes at 4 PM, and the area in front of the Aviation Museum BOON closes at 5 PM. 2023.10.29 (Submitted by: w, October 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: This is one of the few free overnight parking spots in Kobe. There is a flush toilet with a Japanese-style toilet, and space to park about two cars next to it. It is on the road, so use at your own risk. Also, there is almost no cell phone signal. (Submitted by: Kato no Ran, May 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: There is a large parking lot 1 directly below, but this second one is closer to the toilets. The multipurpose toilet seat was broken and unusable, but the one I used had both flush toilets (Western and Japanese style). Actually, even on a Saturday afternoon, there weren't that many people, and I slept more than I expected because it was so quiet (lol). There was no sense that it was closed at night, and the footbath and hot spring facilities were only about a 10-minute drive away, which was very convenient (actually there is a hotel even closer, but day-use bathing is only from 11am to 3pm...). If you only need a shower, the roadside station Rennyo no Sato Awara is close after it opens in April. Hot spring facilities → Centopia Awara (details), footbath → Ashiyu (details) (Posted: March 2023, by yuko)

■Report from our website reader: Opened on December 10, 2017, following the extension of the Shin-Meishin Expressway. Located next to the Ibaraki-Senteiji Interchange, it is possible to exit to the interchange after using the rest area on both the northbound and southbound lanes, but it is not possible to use the rest area after entering from the interchange. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There are coin-operated showers on the northbound side (24-hour operation, 300 yen/10 minutes), and 24-hour convenience stores on both the northbound and southbound sides. (Submitted by: n, September 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: A free, quiet, and clean toilet with a bidet function located in the heart of Obama City. Open 24 hours. Location: 111-1 Obama Shirahige, Obama City, Fukui Prefecture (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A park with tennis courts located behind Komatsu Air Base and the airport. There are no signs prohibiting nighttime use, and it seems easy to use as there are houses, including apartment complexes, across the road. However, according to reviews, "the parking lot may be full or closed during base events," so noise is something to be aware of. The toilets have a bidet and a Japanese-style toilet in the women's restroom only, but the men's restroom only has a Japanese-style toilet, so those who want to use it should be embarrassed...←(The multi-purpose restroom has a regular Western-style flush toilet) It's also a convenient spot as Imaie Onsen is only a 5-minute drive away. (Even if that's closed on Tuesdays, you can go a little further to Kiba Onsen or Katayamazu Onsen) (Posted by: yuko, January 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: There is a small but clean toilet. It is Western-style, flushable, separate for men and women, and has a disabled-accessible toilet. There is also a shower and faucet outside the toilet, which is convenient. You cannot throw away trash. Maruyama, a representative spot of Tenjinzaki, is right in front of the site, making it ideal for photography and fishing. Please note that anglers may be coming and going early in the morning. The parking lot is gravel but spacious. It is clearly visible on Google Street View. The road in front leads to the "Tenjinzaki Motoshima First Parking Lot" on the north side of the cape, but there are several places where the road is narrow and it is difficult for vehicles to pass each other. (Submitted by tossan in October 2023)

■Report from our site's readers: A temporary parking lot mainly for users of the Shinhotaka Ropeway. There are toilets and it's cool even in summer. *Caution is needed when security guards are present in the summer. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Although it was posted as a spot where overnight parking is permitted, when I visited yesterday (October 15, 2019), there was a sign prohibiting overnight parking and prolonged stays in vehicles, so overnight parking is not possible.

■[Weekdays] Maximum 1200 yen from 7 AM to midnight, [Weekends] Maximum 1500 yen from 7 AM to midnight, maximum 500 yen from midnight to 7 AM. There is a toilet on the first floor, and overnight parking is permitted.

■Report from a reader of this site: The car camping map indicated that there was a toilet and that car camping was possible, so I car camped there on December 21st (Tuesday). I went to the toilet around 2:30 AM, but it was locked and unusable. What a shock! (Submitted: December 2021, Anonymous)

■First hour: 200 yen, 100 yen for each subsequent hour. Fee details: There is a toilet and it has been reported that car camping is possible. For example, if you enter at 7 PM and leave at 8 AM the next morning, it would cost 1400 yen.

■Report from our site's reader: Recommended because there are few cars parked overnight. However, cell phone reception is poor. There are only a few places to shop, such as the Lawson at Kii-Yura Station or A-Coop, so shopping before going to the roadside station is essential. There is a risk of tsunamis, so evacuate to the youth center in the event of an earthquake. (Older post from before 2019)
■Attached auto campsite (showers available): Price details

■Report from our site's reader: Actually, there's a pool with a gym (details) located a little further away within the park grounds. Gym use alone is always a very cheap 100 yen for 2 hours, and it seems showers are also available afterward. The pool is 200 yen in July and August (double at 400 yen at other times), but it has a warming bath (like a regular bath), making it a hidden gem. (Submitted by yuko, October 2023)

■Free parking and public toilets. Confirmed they are not closed at night. It's a vast park with parking lots scattered throughout. It's easy to understand using the aerial photo map. Confirmed that the toilets here (flush toilet, Japanese style) and here (flush toilet, Western style) are available at night. Safety is at your own risk. Mobile phone reception is OK. (Confirmed on-site by administrator, May 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: A parking lot close to the Nanao-Shiroyama Interchange. It looks small from the outside, but there is a vast parking area behind the building with the toilets and rest area. The toilets have clean bidet toilets and are quite new and in perfect working order. There is some traffic in the morning, but I think it is probably very quiet at night. There is also a convenience store nearby, making it fairly convenient. (Submitted by yuko in September 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's very quiet except in front of the vending machines. There are men's, women's, and multi-purpose (flush Western-style) toilets at the back that are available 24 hours a day. The women's toilet is a flush Japanese-style toilet (I don't know about the men's toilet). During business hours, you can also use the toilets inside the store and the women's-only toilet at the back (which has a flush Western-style toilet). There is no parking space for large trucks. Please note that the large parking lot on the north side is for Takihara Shrine, so do not use it. (Submitted by: s, October 2021)
■Report from our website reader: A chain restaurant originating in Shiga Prefecture, famous for its Omi Chanpon. Details on Tabelog (Posted by: n, September 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: My recommendation is "Michi-no-Eki Mino-Shirakawa" (Roadside Station Mino-Shirakawa). It's located along National Route 41, but because it's in a mountainous area, there isn't much traffic at night. My recommended spot for overnight parking is near the pedestrian overpass in the second parking lot. You can get good Wi-Fi reception inside your car there. Furthermore, there is a small toilet in the second parking lot that can be used at night. This toilet is always kept clean and well-maintained. There aren't many people using the second parking lot at night, so I recommend it. (Submitted by: t, April 2022)
■Report from a reader of this site: I used the municipal parking lot. It had restrooms, and the maximum charge for 24 hours was 1500 yen. Details (Submitted by: j, April 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Located across from Yokkaichi Oiwake Post Office, between National Route 1 and Mie Prefectural Road 407. This location is also designated as a Mie Prefecture monument (historic site) as "Hinaga no Oiwake".
■Report from our website reader: A rice ball specialty shop originating in Yokkaichi City. Details on Tabelog (Posted: June 2025, by user n)

■Report from a reader of this site: Regarding the Sanyo Expressway, Ogo PA (downbound). Visited on a Saturday in May 2023. There are many spaces for large vehicles, so the risk of trucks entering the small vehicle area seems low. There is also a restaurant and a convenience store. EV Quick is available. (Submitted by: n, May 2023)

■Coin showers available in both directions. 24 hours, 300 yen/10 minutes

■Report from a reader of this site: It's a small station in the mountains. It's along a main road, but traffic is light. There are two clean toilets with bidet functions. There's nothing nearby. The air is clean, and I think you can see the starry sky well on a clear day. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, June 2021)

■Report from a reader of this site: As it is located on a mountain slope, the road surface is inevitably a little sloped, but the toilets (I think there might not be any bidets...) are usable even at night, and the parking lot lights are on. As it is a parking lot set up on the mountainside to view Takeda Castle, a castle ruin in the sky located several kilometers away, it is naturally quiet. When I told the local tourist information center that I wanted to see Takeda Castle floating in a sea of ​​clouds, they advised me to go to the above parking lot at night and climb to the observation deck before dawn to avoid the crowds. Therefore, I think overnight stays in cars are permitted. The nearest hot spring is Yofudo Onsen, about a 10-minute drive away (details). I used it in the autumn when the probability of a sea of ​​clouds appearing is high, so if you plan to use it at other times of the year, you should check with the tourist information center. (Even though I used it on a Sunday night, the parking lot was full by 3 a.m. the next morning.) Most recently, I stayed from October 22-23, 2023. (Posted: August 2025, MO from Chiba Prefecture)
■Free parking and portable toilets are available. Many people are staying overnight in their cars to photograph Takeda Castle. There are also some people who idle their engines excessively, so it's best to keep your distance from them. Sedans usually idle until morning. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: I was just at Celepark 18-jo Higashi in Osaka. I went to Kitajima Shin Onsen (520 yen, details). (Posted: May 2024, by t)
■Coin parking. A hidden gem for overnight stays in your car in Osaka. Adjacent to public toilets! Very cheap at a maximum of 600 yen for 24 hours (Note: Maximum charge is only for one time)! 10-minute walk to Higashimikuni Subway Station! (Accessible to Umeda and Namba by train.) Adjacent to a police box, so no troublemakers gather! (A double-edged sword as you might get stopped and questioned by the police.) How about using it as a base for sightseeing in Osaka? It seems pretty good. It's too hot in the summer, so it's not suitable. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's located along the national highway bypass, so it gets very crowded and noisy. I recommend Totto Park Kotori instead. (Older post from before 2019)
■Opened on April 1, 2017. A roadside station/parking area on the national highway bypass.

■Report from our site's reader: It faces a national highway but traffic is light. It's a rural area surrounded by orchards. There are 24-hour washlet toilets. Pear picking, grape picking, and peach picking (planned). Currently, peaches and cherry blossoms are in full bloom, and harvesting will take place in the fall. Large vehicles can also be parked. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, March 2021)

■Report from a reader of this site: This is a free parking lot located between National Route 249 and Nakai Bay. There are 18 parking spaces for regular cars and 4 for large vehicles. It slopes downwards towards the sea, but it is very gentle so I don't think it will be a problem. Clean toilets are available 24 hours a day and were cleaned around 5:30 a.m. Men: 3 urinals/2 stalls, Women: 5 stalls, Accessible: 1 stall. All have bidet toilets, and both the toilet seats and the flushing water are heated. I was the only one staying overnight in my car this time, but there are four streetlights so it was bright and I didn't feel unsafe at all. There is almost no traffic at night, so I was able to stay overnight in my car in a quiet and comfortable environment. Initially, I had planned to stay overnight in my car at Michi-no-Eki Anamizu. Michi-no-Eki Anamizu is attached to Anamizu Station on the Noto Railway, and the distinction between the parking lot for the roadside station and the train station is unclear. If you are staying overnight in a campervan or van, you will be very concerned about the eyes of station users, so I recommend this parking lot if you are staying overnight in Anamizu. There are several parking lots of this kind on the Noto Peninsula, so I thought it was a good place to stay overnight in a car. (Posted by Mr. Y in October 2020)
■Report from our site's reader: South of the Gifu Bypass on National Route 21. It's in the middle of rice fields, but parking is prohibited in the surrounding area.
■Report from our website reader: The restaurant where Takayama ramen originated. (Reviewed on Tabelog in September 2024 by user n)

■Report from our site's reader: Spacious and deserted, but the toilets are somewhat dilapidated (Submitted by: Kousagi, May 2025)
■Free parking and toilets. It's quiet with little traffic. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: It was said that the large parking lot was quiet and nice in the back, but recently a pharmacy was built on the premises, and now parking is only possible near the road. I decided against car camping, but I tried parking there and I think it wouldn't be very comfortable due to the noise of cars driving by. (Submitted by: M, October 2022)

■Surprisingly, car camping is possible next to a public toilet. 100 yen for 60 minutes from 8 PM to 8 AM, 1800 yen maximum for 24 hours. The toilet acts like a soundproof wall, and the back is quiet and quite nice. The station is also very close. A public bath (Izumi-yu) is within walking distance. (Kyoto car camping spot)

■Report from our site's reader: This is the parking lot of a sports park with a baseball field and tennis courts located within an industrial park. There is another parking lot, but cars can also be parked here, and across the walkway there are separate men's and women's restrooms that are open 24 hours and have no external locks on the entrance. Both stalls have bidet toilets and are relatively clean. It is located somewhat close to the national highway, but it may be quiet at night if the factories are not operating... (I was there around 8am, and it was noisy with trucks then...) (Submitted by yuko, June 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Across the street is a complex called Rapia Kashima, and its parking lot is probably usable as it is not chained or locked (if it is open, you can also use the toilets there which have bidet toilets, and it is definitely usable until the library inside closes at 7pm). Further on, there are men's, women's, and multipurpose toilets in the park, but those are just regular flush toilets. It is also quite close to "Orihime no Sato Nakanoto," and is recommended for those who are more concerned with the surrounding noise than the toilets. (Rapia Kashima is behind the Alplaza supermarket) (Submitted by yuko in November 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: One of the few tourist spots on the west side of Lake Biwa. It's a good place to visit before or after visiting Shirahige Shrine. There is a Manyoshu poetry monument on the edge of the pond. The wooden bridge in the middle of the pond alone is Instagrammable. There is a free parking lot with space for 5 cars on the west side of the pond (with a restroom). The directions to the parking lot are difficult to find, so it's a good idea to check your navigation system in advance. (Submitted by: Kuu-kun, October 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: Currently, due to construction work until May, the parking space is narrower. I came during the daytime, but the construction noise was loud (this can be blocked with noise-canceling earphones, headphones, or earplugs; I slept soundly with them, especially after eating). It doesn't look like the entrance will be closed at night. There are toilets with automatic lighting inside the site about 80m away, with Western-style (heated seats), Japanese-style, and bidet toilets. (Submitted by yuko in March 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: This sports park is located a little off the prefectural road. There were bollards to stop cars, but they didn't seem to be in use, and it didn't look like it would be closed at night. The toilets are across the park path; the regular ones are Western-style flush toilets, but the multi-purpose ones have bidet toilets. There is a footbath a short drive away, and several hot spring baths nearby. (Submitted by yuko in May 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Behind the building is the boarding and alighting point for the Fugan Water Line, and there is an automatically lit toilet in the passageway leading there. The toilet is a regular Western-style flush toilet, but there is a FamilyMart across the street where you can use a bidet. If you go a little further, you will find Hikatae Onsen (12:00-21:00, closed Wednesdays, 470 yen, details, official website), and even further on is Gokuraku no Yu (large rest room available, 470 yen, details, official website) where you can draw drinkable spring water. (Submitted by: yuko, September 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: The view is amazing, and there are four parking lots (1-4), so it's easy to move around. There are measures in place to deter biker gangs. It's also at a good altitude, so it's cool enough to sleep in (239m above sea level). (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: It seems the facility has been renovated recently, and the 24-hour public toilets are incredibly clean. What's more, you can see the night view from inside the public toilets. The city seems to be putting effort into promoting it as a night view spot, and the paved walkway to the observation deck sparkles with something like black light, making it very beautiful. However, the downside is that there are no public baths in Tahara City, so you have to bathe in neighboring Toyohashi City or somewhere similar before going. *As it's a night view spot, there's a possibility that a lot of delinquents will gather there on weekends. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Reader Report: Docomo mobile phone service is available, but Softbank service is not. There is a sign asking people to turn off the lights in the toilets when not in use at night. The men's toilet is Japanese style, the multi-purpose toilet is Western style, and the women's toilet has a bidet. I was the only user at night. (Submitted by: A, August 2024)
■ Free parking and toilets. This is Gifu Prefecture, right on the border. (Older post from before 2019)
■ Reader Report: It's too lonely at night because it's in the mountains, but there are clean toilets! (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Mobile phone signal is almost fine for au, but barely for Docomo. It has a bidet function, but the crucial function didn't work at all... so mysterious. (Submitted by yuko, September 2023)

■Free parking and public toilets. Confirmed not to be closed at night. Although it's in the mountains, the parking lot is level and flat. The toilets seem to have been renovated recently, and I was surprised to find a flush toilet with a bidet in such a location. Mobile phone signal is barely OK. Very quiet at night. Safety is at your own risk. Elevation 273m. (Confirmed on-site by administrator in May 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: I used this when I went to see the Gujo Odori dance festival. It's an Akippa reserved parking lot (details). I reserved it for two days because I was going to stay overnight in my car. It's very convenient because it's a convenience store parking lot. The fee is 1200 yen plus tax for two days. (Posted by TOM in August 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a large free parking lot (free of charge) just before the Chikatsuyu Art Museum, and the restrooms are clean. It is generally quiet, but especially quiet along the river. There is a hot spring called Hisui-no-Yu 600m to the north, but be sure to check the opening hours. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There's a McDonald's nearby, but it's about the same price, and this is far better. You can get extra fries for an extra 100 yen on top of the set, and you'll be full. Tabelog

■Report from a reader of this site: A massive monolith, designated as a cultural property (natural monument and scenic spot) by Kyoto Prefecture. It is augite andesite, formed when magma cooled and solidified. It is a giant rock with columnar cracks, exhibiting a columnar jointing structure. It can be reached on foot via a sandbar and a tombolo. Attached images 1, 2, and 3 (Submitted by: s, September 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking space is relatively large for its size. There is a slight gap between the parking spaces for large vehicles and regular vehicles. It is located along a national highway intersection, but traffic is relatively light. There is a convenience store on the corner of the intersection. Large vehicles do come by, but it wasn't too noisy. There is a table in front of the restrooms. (Submitted by c, June 2024)

■Reader Report: Regarding the Okuise Parking Area on the northbound Kisei Expressway. The facilities are new, and the restrooms are clean. There are vending machines. There is also an EV fast charger. Traffic is light and it is quiet. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Reader Report: Correction to Existing Article (Likely Not Allowed for Overnight Parking) As shown in the second image (attached image), it appears to be closed at night. (Something resembling a car barrier was also visible.) Note that the other Ataka-no-Seki parking lot on the side with the FamilyMart (details) does not seem to be closed at night. (Toilets include flush toilets (Japanese and Western style), and the multi-purpose toilet is also a regular flush toilet (Western style)) (Submitted: April 2023, yuko)

■ Reader Report: Free Parking (100 regular cars) and Toilets. A park located at the site of Ataka-no-Seki, famous from the Kabuki play "Kanjincho." It seems like a quiet location where one could spend a comfortable night, but the poster only visited during the day, so details are unknown. (Submitted: November 2021, y)
■Report from our website reader: A restaurant serving Gifu's specialty, "Gifu Tanmen." (Reviewed on Tabelog in March 2022 by user n)

■Report from our website reader: There is a water refill station (24 hours) at the Shizumo Roadside Station in Gifu where you can get Shizumo Shimizu water. It seems they use the same water that the roadside station uses.

■Report from our website reader: This spring is located in Tochiharaguchi Pocket Park along Prefectural Road 17, which runs from Eiheiji Temple towards Katsuyama City, following the Kuzuryu River from Maruoka Town. The source of the spring is at the seventh station of Washigatake Mountain, and it is said that the locals have come to call it "Tantan Shimizu" (Tantan Spring) because it gushes out with a gentle tapping sound at the water source in the small park. It is also known as "Tochihara no Urikari Shimizu" (Tochihara's Melon Splitting Spring). It seems that many drivers make the effort to take the prefectural road from National Route 416 just to get this spring. (Submitted by: Y, October 2020)
■Report from our site's readers: This coffee shop is famous for serving unusual dishes such as sweet matcha red bean spaghetti. There is parking available for about 10 cars. (Tabelog)

■Report from our website reader: Located in the city center, the parking lot is crowded, making it impossible to get a good night's sleep. Wi-Fi available from 8:00 to 19:00. Closed on Wednesdays (irregular closures). (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A parking lot with a ramp leading to the sea. It's quite spacious. However, there are no toilets. Unlike the area separated by a gate at the end of the road, this area is not subject to closure, and judging from the prohibited items (attached image), it seems that normal overnight stays in a car are not a problem. If you need a toilet, it is recommended to go back a little towards the Shinminato Bridge. 👉️Details (Posted: April 2022, by yuko)

■Report from our site's reader: Only a temporary toilet is available. The store is closed. If you're okay with just a temporary toilet, you can stay overnight in your car. (Submitted by: Kousagi, May 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking area for local roads has a small sign asking people to refrain from parking for extended periods. The downhill side has only a few spaces and seems to be shared with commercial use. The uphill side has more spaces but is on a slope, and the entrance from Prefectural Road 622 is difficult to find. It's quiet as it's separate from the service area parking lot. There's a convenience store nearby. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Regarding the southbound side. Used on a weekday in July 2025. I was prepared for it to be extremely crowded because it's a small rest area, but surprisingly, it was about half empty. The parking space just before the main parking lot (the approach area) is quieter. I had breakfast at Matsuya, which is open 24 hours. It's filling and cheap, great! (Submitted by: n, July 2025)

■Reader Report: Regarding the southbound side. Used on a Sunday in November 2023. A large-scale service area on the Chugoku Expressway. There weren't many large vehicles, so it was fairly quiet. There's an EV Quick at the western end of the parking lot. (Posted by: n, November 2023)

■Spacious service area, relatively quiet. The far left side is good because trucks don't come easily. Recommended here. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There are coin showers on the southbound side (24-hour operation, 400 yen/20 minutes, details available). There are 24-hour convenience stores and food courts on both the northbound and southbound sides. (Posted by: m, October 2022)
■I stayed overnight in my car at the "Plat Park" on the southbound side. It's behind the highway service area building, so the idling noise of trucks is blocked out, making it quiet and fantastic. I slept soundly until morning with earplugs in. The toilets are incredibly clean. This place is the best. I've added it to my favorites. However, the service area is full of trucks, and the idling noise is tremendous. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: The ultimate spot with a hot spring facility right next door. (Noto Nanami Health and Welfare Village "Nagomi" *Closed due to the 2024 earthquake) The attached toilets are flush toilets with bidet functions. It might be nice to arrive early, park close to the facility, get ready, go to the bath, and then drink your fill at the restaurant, which has a last order at 7:30 PM. (Submitted by yuko in May 2023)
■Report from our website reader: Business reopens, toilets available 24 hours a day, serves as a resting place for volunteers during the day (Submitted by: Kousagi, May 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: The parking lot at the multi-purpose field in the sports park is open even at night. There are signs saying "Camping (overnight stays) in tents is prohibited in the park," but there is no mention of sleeping in cars. The toilets have bidet functions. There is a delicious ramen shop nearby that is open in the mornings. (Submitted by yuko, April 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: The location is almost right next to the city's crematorium, and the parking lot is open after 5 pm, so there are no nighttime closures. The toilets are Western-style flush toilets, and the facility is relatively new, having been built in the last few years, so it's clean. It's a little further from National Route 8, so it's quieter than a roadside station. It's a surprisingly good location, close to a 7-Eleven, Lawson, and a public bathhouse. It might get noisy in the mornings depending on the weather, though... (Submitted by yuko, April 2023)
■Report from our website's readers: Approximately 3km from the intersection on Aichi Prefectural Road 377. Take the narrow road from the intersection near Okazaki City Firefly School.
■Report from a reader of this site: Located along Aichi Prefectural Road 35, about 1km west from the intersection with National Route 473 (there is a bus stop and many flags as landmarks).

■ Reader Report: The restaurant closes at 4 PM, and the cafe attached to Montbell closes at 7 PM. Clean toilets are available 24 hours a day. Why is the RV park the furthest from the toilets? (Submitted by: a, October 2025)
■ Reader Report: This roadside station has a vast parking lot, and at night only about a third of the streetlights in the parking lot are lit, so it's dark and comfortable near the roadside station building. The parking area for trucks is separated, and the sound of trucks idling wasn't too bothersome. Also, although there is an expressway nearby, the traffic volume is very low day and night, making you wonder if there was any point in building the expressway. The downside is that once the roadside station closes, there are no convenience stores, restaurants, or public baths nearby (about 8 km away). (Submitted by: Yamabiko, September 2024)
■ Reader Report: A recently built roadside station. The operating hours are short, from 9 AM to 6 PM. There is also a paid parking area where you can pitch tents and there are power outlets. (Submitted by: h, February 2024)
■Report from our site's reader: A vast parking lot completely separated from Route 158. You can spend a comfortable night there. (Submitted by: y, November 2021)
■Grand opening on April 22, 2021. RV park available. Overall map

■Report from our website reader: A parking lot adjacent to the museum that is open to everyone. It's quiet as it's set back from the main road. There are toilets on the premises, but it's unclear if they are available 24 hours a day. The toilets are clean and have bidet functions. There is a 7-Eleven within 50 meters. (Submitted by: g, November 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: The map shows a 24-hour rate of 800 yen, but when I went today, it had been revised to 12 hours for 1000 yen. (Submitted by: Sunagon, June 2024)
■15-minute walk to Sannomiya. A short walk to the south is needed for public restrooms (including flush toilets) in the adjacent "Minato-no-Mori Park (Kobe Earthquake Reconstruction Memorial Park)" (details). Detailed report (2020)

■Report from our site's readers: Details of the Metasequoia Avenue in Makino Highlands The scenery of approximately 500 metasequoia trees planted on both sides of a 2.4km straight road has become a hot topic on social media, etc. Please be mindful of manners, as on-street parking and taking photos in the middle of the road have become a problem.

■Report from a reader of this site: Parking lot across the road from Furusato Nishibetsuin. We have received permission from Furusato Nishibetsuin to allow overnight parking in vehicles. There are no toilets. There are vending machines. A convenience store is a five-minute drive away. There is no shade in the parking lot. The ground is level. If you park at the back of the parking lot, the noise from cars is not too bothersome. You can also buy delicious eggs and vegetables in the morning. (Submitted by: y, August 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: I used the Fishing Sanctuary for overnight stays in my car the day before tournaments such as the Trout King Championship. I think the area further back, closer to the toilets and not too brightly lit, is a good place to sleep. The toilets are dark at night unless you turn on the light switch. (Submitted by: Fishing Berserker, February 2026)

■Report from a reader of this site: The Ataka-no-Seki parking lot on the side with the FamilyMart does not appear to be closed at night. (The toilets include flush toilets (Japanese and Western style), and the multi-purpose toilet is also a regular flush toilet (Western style)) (Submitted by yuko in April 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Thanks to the bypass, it's relatively quiet at night, but the parking lot is small, so it's recommended to sleep in the parking lot across the river, even though it's further from the toilets. (Older post from before 2019)
■Opened August 11, 2017.

■Report from a reader of this site: I think it's OK outside of peak season. There are toilets and running water, so it's safe. There is a public hot spring and a supermarket nearby, which is very convenient. However, it seems that some young people were vandalizing the vending machines the night we were staying in our car, so caution is advised. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Reader Report: It's in the middle of nowhere, but noisy because it's along the road (Older post from before 2019)
■ Reader Report: I stayed overnight in my car at the Amarube roadside station. I wasn't keen on going because there was a major accident there in the past, but it was a quiet night with nothing happening. The toilets were well-maintained and clean. It's along the coast, so it's good for a walk. Perhaps because it was a weekday, there were hardly any cars, so I was able to relax. There's an observation deck at the Sky Station right nearby, and the view is fantastic. It's also good to take the train from Amarube Station and come back right away. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: The truck parking area is somewhat far away, so the noise isn't too bothersome. There's a 24-hour convenience store, a 24-hour gyudon (beef bowl) restaurant on the northbound lane, and a food court (7:00 AM - 10:00 PM) offering "Nagoya cuisine" on the southbound lane. [Plat Park for local roads, 24-hour OK] (Older post from before 2019)

■Plat Park is available 24 hours a day on both the northbound and southbound lanes. WiMAX signal is available on both lanes. The northbound side is noisy with a lot of coming and going until late at night because there's a convenience store. The southbound side also has a lot of coming and going. Not really recommended. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: There are toilets. At night, it's mostly just cars belonging to people night fishing or couples. However, it gets full of fishing cars from before dawn, so you need to be able to tolerate that. There is a risk of tsunamis, so be sure to check evacuation routes so you can escape quickly. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Free parking lot with attached toilets. The multi-purpose toilet was a regular flush Western-style toilet, and I believe the separate men's and women's toilets were flush Japanese-style toilets. (Submitted by yuko, April 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: It's a parking lot with toilets, and there were quite a few cars parked there before 9am. The toilets are recycled flush toilets (the type where water runs continuously), and the multi-purpose toilet has a heated seat. It doesn't seem entirely unsuitable for overnight stays in a car, but it's not very spacious, so it's a bit questionable. (Submitted by yuko, April 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: I saw that the toilets were Japanese-style flush toilets and had bidet functions. (Submitted by yuko, June 2023)
■Free parking and public toilets. Confirmed that they are not closed at night. The toilets are clean flush toilets, and there are also Western-style toilets. Cell phone reception is OK. Very quiet at night. A hidden gem. Safety is at your own risk. (Administrator's on-site verification, June 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: Good toilets, very good Wi-Fi, good scenery, Meihō Onsen is heated water so I didn't go in, the national highway has little traffic and hardly any large vehicles. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, June 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: The toilet had a bidet, which was nice, but it was noisy, probably due to the trucks. (Visited in the evening, not at night) However, the soft serve ice cream at Kinoko no Sato right in front is delicious (eat outside or take out). Nearby is Hanibe Gankutsuin, a place visited by Rantime (see video for details). The fact that there's a bathing facility (Pure Yusenji, 490 yen, details) quite close by is convenient... (Posted: October 2023, by yuko)

■Free parking, toilets available, noisy due to being along a main road (older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Although it says that the toilets have bidets, there were no bidets in the multi-purpose toilet, men's toilet, or on the north or east side. Confirmed on May 2, 2025. (Submitted by: x, May 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is also a north parking lot in front of a convenience store along the prefectural road (no noticeable tilt), but this location in front of the hospital, further away, is slightly quieter. The toilets have Western-style flush toilets and bidets (same for the north side). However, while there wasn't much of a noticeable tilt near the toilets here, there are places where you can feel the tilt towards the prefectural road. (Submitted by: yuko, April 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: There are toilets and a few parking spaces... but that area has a strong slope to the side and is not suitable for sleeping. What I would recommend is the large parking lot by the river down the path? It seems to be a good place as it is not sloped. There is a railway bridge almost directly next to it. The toilets are flush toilets, both Japanese and Western style, but the Western style toilet in the women's toilet is broken, and the others are only multi-purpose Western style toilets. Within a few minutes' drive there are water-collecting spots (Ohama water, Hasuike water), hot springs (Yasumaru no Yu and Mikawa Onsen Motoyu Honda), convenience stores and drugstores, so it is surprisingly convenient. (Submitted by yuko in April 2023)

■Reader Report: Toilet with Washlet 2. No matter where you park your car, the toilet is far away. An inconvenient roadside station. The stream is beautiful though. (Submitted by: Migratory Bird Travelogue, June 2021)
■Report from our site's readers: Toilets available. Free parking. Benches available. Great view from Lake Biwa. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Toilets: Flush toilets. Wi-Fi: Coca-Cola vending machine; password required, password is displayed on the vending machine. The vending machine is next to the toilets. (Details), attached image (Submitted by: n, October 2023)

■Report from our site's readers: The supermarket at Mipple shopping mall is open until 9:30 PM. There's a Lawson convenience store about a 5-minute walk south. There's a McDonald's to the west, but it's open until 11:00 PM. There were flyers posted prohibiting long-term overnight stays in vehicles, possibly due to disruptive behavior (electricity theft, theft) by long-term overnight stays. I think it would be fine if you come outside of business hours and clean up before the delivery company arrives (before 7 PM), but let's follow the rules and manners. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's readers: Michi-no-Eki Umi no Kyoto Miyazu. The parking lot itself has limited space. The restaurant at the adjacent Mipple shopping mall is open from 11 AM to 11 PM. There is a hot spring facility on the grounds of Amanohashidate Station, a five-minute drive away (after 5 PM, the nearby Chionji Temple parking lot becomes free and can be used). (Older post from before 2019)
■Opened in November 2015.
■Report from our site's readers: Details of Sazareishi Park "Sazareishi" is the "small pebbles" sung about in the Japanese national anthem, "Kimigayo".

■Report from our site's readers: Surfer-favorite parking lots. Most parking lots cost 1000 yen/day. Water is free, but be careful as it may be well water. Many places are unmanned from night to morning, so it is possible to park overnight in your car for free. Many places have toilets. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's reader: A parking lot frequented by surfers, 1000 yen/day during the summer only, with toilets available (older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's readers: A parking lot frequented by surfers. Toilets available. There might have been free showers in the summer? (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There's a convenience store. The parking lot is surprisingly spacious. There's also a smart interchange, but facility use is not possible when entering/exiting from the smart interchange. There are trash cans for combustible waste (it seems that trash cans at rest areas on the Maizuru-Wakasa Expressway often only accept cans and plastic bottles to deter wild birds) (Submitted by: C, May 2024)
■Opened on 2014/7/20!

■Report from a reader of this site: A parking lot in a plaza with a golf course and a campsite (there are auto campsites, but they are expensive...). There don't seem to be any wheel stops, so it looks like it could be used at night, but the details are unclear. There is one toilet with a bidet at the back, and the others are flush toilets, both Western and Japanese style. It is also quite close to Ataka PA (ETC-only IC). (Submitted by yuko in April 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: This is a popular spot with a gibier (wild game) cafe attached, and a great view of the sea across the road. There's a sign that says "Please turn off your engine when parking overnight," so it seems that overnight stays in cars are expected. The toilet had a bidet, but the bidet function itself could only be used for multi-purpose use (the power wasn't on) (Submitted by yuko in May 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: A park near Cosmo Isle Hakui (a complex facility housing a space science museum and library, which Rantime also visited). Based on a daytime visit, it's not extremely noisy when there's no traffic, and there isn't much traffic. It's probably quite quiet at night. The fact that the toilets have bidet functions is a big plus. There's a martial arts hall nearby, and even people from outside the city can use the training room until around 10 pm for 150 yen. (Submitted by yuko, October 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: This is a small park. There are toilets. There isn't much traffic, so it's quiet and you can sleep well. It's a great place to go to Nachi! *The nearby "Yatagarasu no Yu" hot spring is closed indefinitely (older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There are clean toilets. There are no streetlights. It's a quiet place to relax. The only thing to note is that the road leading to the location is a bit narrow. Because it's a trailhead, hikers come to park their cars there early in the morning on weekends and holidays. (Submitted by: User 2, May 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: A fairly small roadside station. No signs prohibiting parking for more than 2 hours were found. However, there are houses very close by, and concerns about residents watching out for overnight parking are a concern. (Submitted by zil415, May 2024)
■There is a sign prohibiting parking for more than 2 hours. (Information provided by a reader of this site: i, September 2021)
■A small roadside station in the middle of town. The parking lot is away from the main road and is relatively quiet, which is not bad. (Confirmed on-site by administrator in October 2020)
■Report from our website reader: A restaurant in Gifu that serves "Ankake Katsudon," a dish of pork cutlet topped with a thick egg sauce. Details on Tabelog (Posted by: n, April 2025)

■Reader Report: Regarding the bath, it's conveniently located about a 10-minute walk from Apa Spa Fukui Katamachi (APA Hotel Fukui Katamachi) (details). (6am-24pm, last entry 11:30pm, 1000 yen...but accepts the hot spring passport) (Posted: February 2024, by yuko)

■Overnight stay in a car in the center of Fukui. 1pm-8am the next morning, maximum 500 yen. There is a toilet (flush toilet, Japanese style) on the first floor that can be used at night. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: It appears the auto campsite has been closed. It is unclear whether regular overnight stays in vehicles are permitted in the parking lot. Details: "Camping and BBQ permanently banned at Kasugawa Auto Campsite in Ibigawa Town" (Submitted by h, April 2022)

■Report from our website readers: Details of Ebisenbei no Sato Kariya Oasis Store) Located next to the Kariya PA on the Ise Bay Expressway, but also accessible from local roads. This is the closest store to Nagoya to "Ebisenbei no Sato," a manufacturer of Aichi's famous shrimp crackers. You can sample the shrimp crackers here. Open from 7:00 to 22:00.

■Report from our site's readers: There is a restroom attached to "Irori Chaya Ayu no Sho" a 2-minute walk away, where you can watch ayu (sweetfish) being grilled over a hearth. For details, there is a hot spring facility called "Etchu Shogawa-so" on the opposite bank a 15-minute walk away where you can enjoy a day trip to the baths (older post from before 2019).

■Report from our site's readers: Restrooms and a gazebo are available. Seasonal cuisine restaurant "Uoyasu" is a 2-minute walk away. Details: You can enjoy various dishes depending on the season, but the ayu (sweetfish) rice porridge during ayu season is outstanding (older post from before 2019).

■Report from our site's reader: The service area itself is quite narrow, and you have to be careful when entering and exiting the parking lot. The traffic volume is high, and it's quite close to the main road, so it's not suitable for overnight stays in your car. The fact that the parking spaces for large vehicles and regular vehicles are separated by a building is the only positive point. (Submitted by c, June 2024)

■ Reader Report: When using the restrooms from the general road side outside of SA operating hours, it is possible to access the restrooms from the entrance outside the building. There was a sign indicating that overnight parking is prohibited on the general road side. (Confirmed 2025/6/1) (Submitted by: c, June 2025)

■ Reader Report: Essentially a service area on the Bantan Expressway. Facilities are located on the southbound side, while the northbound side has restrooms and vending machines. Facilities can also be accessed from the general road side. At night, the facilities are closed, so only restrooms and vending machines are available on the Bantan Expressway side, and only the parking lot is usable on the general road side. There are many users, but not many parking spaces. It is close to the main road, and there is a fair amount of traffic. It is not suitable for overnight parking on the general road side. (Submitted by: c, June 2024)

■Report from our website reader: This is the most easily accessible water source from Route 8, located 1.2km towards the sea. Water quality tests are conducted, and it is safe to drink. There is a free parking lot at the station right in front of the water source. Details (Posted by tossan, January 2026)

■ Reader Report: This roadside station was rated A, but there was a sign prohibiting overnight parking, so I moved to another roadside station. (Older post from before 2019)
■ Reader Report: "Spa Miki" is located inside "Hotel Miki," about a 5-minute drive from the roadside station. Previously, there was a bathing facility inside the Mase roadside station, but it has closed and is now a footbath. There is also a sign prohibiting overnight parking. The facility is very clean. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: 900 yen, details. It's a heated, circulating hot spring, not a free-flowing one. The opening hours are longer than nearby hot spring resorts. The restaurant seems to be of good quality.

■Report from our website reader: 800 yen, details available, 100 yen discount with JAF membership card. It's located over a mountain from the national highway. There are no shops nearby. If you head towards the national highway from the hot spring at night, you can see the illuminated Takeda Castle ruins. (Submitted by: c, June 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: 530 yen, details. For this price, you get a spacious rest area (with a TV and a smaller one without), a cafeteria, and a ramen shop inside the building, plus rinse-in shampoo and body soap! (Submitted by yuko, April 2023)
■Super public bath "Matsuto Kaihin Onsen". Within walking distance from Tokumitsu PA.
■Report from our website reader: 500 yen, details. Hot spring hotel with moor spring water; bring your own amenities. (Submitted by: yuko, April 2023)
■Report from our website reader: 460 yen, details. Hot, free-flowing moor spring water, bring your own amenities. (Submitted by: yuko, April 2023)

■Report from our website reader: I'd like to share my experience of staying overnight in my car at "Michi-no-Eki Mokkuru Shinshiro" in Shinshiro City, Aichi Prefecture on March 23rd. Overall, it wasn't bad; the facilities and location were good, and although there was some road noise, there wasn't much truck engine noise on the day, and there were no signs prohibiting overnight parking. However, near the toilets and tourist information center, announcements about events and prohibiting inconsiderate long-term parking were broadcast at a fairly loud volume every 15 minutes or so throughout the night. This is clearly a measure against overnight parking, so I wouldn't recommend it. This was the first time I'd encountered such a roadside station in the entire country, so I wanted to report it. (Submitted: March 2025, t)

■Report from our website reader: Free WiFi available. You can occasionally hear trains passing by, but it's generally quiet. There's a convenience store on the premises, but it's not open 24 hours (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM), so be aware. (Older post from before 2019)

■Opened March 2015!

■Report from our site's readers: There are 24-hour restrooms and parking available, and a Lawson convenience store 250m away. However, it is located along National Route 312, which has heavy traffic even at night, so you will be bothered by the noise of passing cars. For early morning climbs to Takeda Castle, using the Takeda Castle parking lot is best. If you want to climb from the station side, head here after waking up. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a 24-hour maximum charge (details on charges), but no information is provided regarding overnight parking. It is closest to Miyagawa Morning Market, and the toilets are available 24 hours a day at "Hida Takayama Tourist Exchange Center Omasa" which is a 1-minute walk away (details). Bathing facilities are available at "Yutopia Inari no Yu" which is about a 15-minute walk away (details) (Posted: July 2025, by a certain happy1 owner)
■Report from a reader of this site: There are toilets that are open 24 hours a day. It's relatively quiet if you go a little later. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Parking lot of a 24-hour supermarket. As can be seen from the aerial photograph, there is a vast parking lot in this area, and it is not closed off at night (there is a sign that says no parking after 9 PM, but there are still many parked cars). The toilets are inside the 24-hour supermarket and have been confirmed to be usable at night. They are clean, Western-style flush toilets with bidet functions. The parking lot at the back is very quiet until the next morning. The downside is that security guards patrol in the early morning and leave notices warning against illegal parking. (Submitted by: Kato no Ran, December 2020)

■Report from a reader of this site: 900 yen for 24 hours. It's a fairly large parking lot, and it's quite quiet if you park away from the main road. Restrooms are available at Kiba Market or nearby convenience stores. Namba is within walking distance, and it's also close to Daikokucho Station, making it easy to get to Umeda. (Submitted by: Eigo, a shrine visitor service provider, November 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking. Slightly flat, gravel, no designated spaces, can accommodate about 7 passenger cars, shade available. 24-hour toilet, Western-style flush toilet, multi-purpose toilet available, no bidet. Vending machine available, no trash cans, bench available. *Visited around 6:30 AM. There were a few visitors. (Submitted by Takora in August 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking, spacious and slightly sloped, few users, shady spots in the morning. 24-hour toilets available, flush toilets (Japanese style) and wheelchair-accessible Western-style toilets, no bidet. There are also toilets and vending machines further inside (closed from 5pm to 8am). Flush toilets (Western style), and the multipurpose toilet has a bidet. Dark and surrounded by nature, with insect sounds. Covered benches and vending machines available, no trash cans. (Submitted by: Takora, July 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking, spacious, flat, gravel, no designated spaces, few users. 24-hour toilets available, lots of insects. Flush toilets, Western style, multipurpose toilet available, no bidet. Dark and quiet, abundant nature so insect repellent needed, birds chirp in the morning. Covered benches and tables available. No vending machines or trash cans. (Submitted by Takora, June 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking, no designated spaces, grassy, ​​flat. 24-hour toilet, Japanese style, doesn't seem to be a flush toilet, water not potable. No trash cans, beware of bears. Visited at 6 AM. Rakuten Mobile service unavailable. There is a chain pole embedded in the ground at the entrance, so it may be closed at times. (Submitted by Takora, August 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: 24-hour free parking, narrow and sloped. 24-hour paid toilets, fee is voluntary (donation), equipped with bidet. Benches and vending machines available. Visited at 8:00 AM. (Submitted by Takora, August 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking, slightly sloped, busy. 24-hour toilets, including a multi-purpose toilet with a bidet. No trash cans, but benches are available. Visited at 7:30 AM. (Submitted by Takora, August 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking, slightly sloped, few users, some shaded spots in the morning. 24-hour toilets available, flush toilets (Japanese style) and wheelchair-accessible Western-style toilets, no bidet. Dark and surrounded by nature, sounds of insects. Covered benches and vending machines available, no trash cans. (Submitted by Takora, July 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 24-hour free parking, slightly sloped, EV charging available. 24-hour toilets, flush toilets (Western style), multi-purpose toilet with bidet. No trash cans, covered benches and tables available. (Submitted by Takora in August 2025)
■Opened in November 2015. It seems to have originally operated as a "town station".

■Report from a reader of this site: 24-hour parking lot for 400 yen, cash only, paved, flat (same conditions for adjacent parking lots), toilet in the park across the street (Japanese style flush toilet, no toilet paper, no lighting) (Submitted by: Takora, February 2026)

■Report from our site's readers: 24:00-8:00, a maximum of only 20 yen for nighttime use. The late start time (midnight) is a drawback. Details (older post from before 2019)
■There is a toilet at the Lawson convenience store about 50m north. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's readers: 24:00-8:00, a maximum of just 10 yen for nighttime use. The late start time (24:00) is a drawback. Details (older post from before 2019)
■There are toilets in the adjacent Lawson convenience store. (older post from before 2019)
