■ Reader Report: Toilets available, free of charge. *Caution regarding heavy snow in winter. It is unclear whether the parking lot is cleared of snow. (Submitted by: h, February 2024)

■Report from our website reader: Weekday dinner in January 2025. After visiting the Ise Kawasaki Merchant House, we used this restaurant while parked in the Merchant House's parking lot with permission. The oyster feast was amazing. The service was also polite. (Submitted by: n, February 2025)

■Report from our website reader: I stayed overnight in my car during Golden Week in 2025. There was little traffic on the road in front, and few cars idling, so it was quiet and I slept well. The toilet was clean. From around 5 AM, the number of visitors (tourists and people receiving deliveries at the roadside station) gradually increased. (Submitted by: t, May 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: Confirmed on site on June 4, 2025. It is located on the access route from the east to Odaigahara from Osugidani. There is a maximum of about 6 parking spaces (see attached image), but it is a very quiet environment. The road in front is National Route 422, but it is essentially a dead end (Prefectural Route 603 that continues further ahead is steep and is often closed due to landslides, etc.), so there are very few passing vehicles. There are toilets with heated bidets, separate Western-style toilets for men and women, a disabled-accessible toilet, and a changing room (see attached image). We confirmed with the Odai Town Hall, the administrator, that it is not closed 24 hours a day. Across the road is the Miyagawa riverbed, and there is a changing room because it is a place where you can play in the water. It will probably be crowded on summer holidays. The adjacent gazebo seems convenient for eating or sheltering from the rain. Also, you can draw fresh water at Sekinotani Park 6.7km downstream. (Submitted by tossan in June 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: 2025-11-04 On-site verification: Located on the banks of the Shogawa River, it's a very quiet place. The toilets in the park are open all day. They are Western-style but do not have bidet seats. They are cleaned every morning and are very clean. The parking area is divided into north and south sections, with the toilets on the north side. The south side has a large roof and wooden deck, which is helpful in rainy weather. Both sides have ample parking space and are flat. Attached images (Posted by tossan, November 2025)

■Reader Report: I also used this parking lot on a weekday in April 2024 when watching a baseball game at Koshien Stadium. Currently, it's a maximum of 600 yen for 24 hours (see attached image). Since it's in front of the station, there are restaurants and convenience stores nearby, and there are toilets outside the station (details) and inside the station (2nd floor). It's close to Koshien and very convenient. (Posted: April 2024, by n)

■Reader Report: Paid coin parking lot near Hanshin Imazu Station. Toilets: Within 100m in the station square! Convenience store: FamilyMart. Bath: There's a public bathhouse about 500m away! (7-minute walk) I used this parking lot when watching the 100th anniversary high school baseball tournament. It's quiet despite being in front of the station, and a 15-minute walk to Koshien Stadium. For popular games, there are long lines, so it's convenient for those who want to line up early. Many cars with out-of-town license plates were seen; it seems to be a popular parking lot! (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: We stayed overnight in our car on January 2nd, 2024. This is a temporary parking lot due to renovations to the large vehicle area at Suzuka PA, so it may only be available for a limited time. The parking areas for large and small vehicles are separated, and there is space for about 15 small vehicles. What you need to be careful about is that it is only on the southbound side of the Tomei-Hanshin Expressway, and there are no electronic signs, so the entrance to the PA is difficult to find, and if you pass it without turning left immediately after entering, you will never be able to park in the small vehicle area again. Details: The toilets are about 200m away, which is a bit inconvenient, but there is no food court or even vending machines, so people who do not intend to take a break (maybe they just missed the entrance?) park directly in front of the toilets, use the facilities, and drive off immediately, so despite it being New Year's, there was no one else there besides us. (There weren't even any large vehicles on the day we stayed overnight, but it seems that the large vehicle area is crowded on weekdays.) The noise from the main road is a bit bothersome, but since all the service areas on the Kansai side are crowded, it might be worth considering. (Posted by: Yasusugi, January 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: September 16, 2024. While parked at Yokoyama Observatory P1 and preparing to camp overnight with the hatchback open, a man came to lock the toilet door around 5:30 PM and asked, "Are you camping here?" When I replied, "I intend to camp overnight," he said, "This is within a national park, so please don't. Please go to a roadside station," and I was unable to camp overnight. (Submitted by: A, September 2024)

■Report from our website reader: Visited on a weekday in November 2023. This is a parking lot (for a few cars) for viewing Tango Matsushima, a famous spot on the Tango Peninsula. There is a restroom. It is located along a main road, but traffic is light. There were about three cars parked there overnight before 8 AM. (Submitted by: n, November 2023)

■Report from our website reader: Used on a weekday in November 2023. A relatively small roadside station. Considering the site area, it should be able to accommodate more vehicles, but the layout means that parking spaces are almost exclusively along the main road. However, the blocks for large vehicles and regular vehicles are separated, which is convenient. There is an EV Quick on the back (south side) of the building. (Submitted by: n, November 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used on a weekday in November 2023. This is a large, combined northbound and southbound service area on the Shin-Meishin Expressway. While many service areas/parking areas have regular car parking spaces located at the back after turning left from the entrance, at this northbound service area, the regular car parking spaces are located straight ahead from the entrance. Be careful, as turning left leads to a passage that returns you to the main road. There are many large trucks here, so it's quite noisy, but earplugs were sufficient. There are EV Quick stations on both the northbound and southbound sides, located near the building after entering from the entrance. (Submitted by: n, November 2023)

■There are a lot of trucks, and it's very noisy. There's no separation from the trucks. It's at an altitude of approximately 300m, so it's cool at night even in summer. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Used on a weekday in November 2023. The parking lot is so vast it's almost bewildering. There's a slope, so consider which way you'll be sleeping when you park. There's a shop and toilets at the top of the stairs at the northern end of the parking lot. There's nothing around, so I was able to rest in silence. There's an EV Quick at the bottom of the stairs. (Posted: November 2023, by n)
■Report from our website reader: Used on August 3, 2023. Toilets: Flush toilets, a little far from the parking lot (about 100m up the stairs). Breakfast: There's a restaurant called "Tamago Kake Gohan Kuiya" that serves all-you-can-eat rice with raw egg, open from 7:00 AM inside the park. (Posted: October 2023, by n)
■Good because it's away from the main road. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our website reader: The parking lot has a slight slope. There are no supermarkets or convenience stores nearby, so you have to do your shopping beforehand or do it inside the park during business hours. (Older posts from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used on a weekday in October 2023. Parked here and watched a baseball game at Koshien! Returned to Sannomiya for a victory celebration and then slept in the car. It's a great deal at a maximum of 700 yen for 24 hours, even though it's only a 10-minute walk from Sannomiya Station (apparently the price was recently lowered). The toilets at Ikutagawa Park, right in front, are 50m away. However, since it's a simple toilet in the park, caution may be needed regarding safety at night (the women's toilet is also open). There was no toilet paper provided. (Submitted by: n, October 2023)

■Discovered a car camping spot in Kobe. There are public toilets in the park across the street. Quiet at night. Maximum of 800 yen for 24 hours, maximum of 400 yen from 8pm to 8am. 11-minute walk to Sannomiya! This is a real hidden gem! (Administrator's on-site verification, October 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: Used on June 13, 2023. Parking available: Two locations on the west and east sides of the park (free). Toilets (flush toilets) are located near the parking lots on the west and east sides of the park. Wi-Fi is available near the toilets on the west and east sides of the park. Streetlights are turned off after 11:00 PM, and Wi-Fi becomes unavailable when the streetlights are off. Re-login is required for Wi-Fi every hour. (Submitted by: n, July 2023)

■Report from our website reader: Used on a weekday in September 2022. The shop and restaurant were closed for renovations until the end of March 2023. The toilets were usable, so I was able to stay overnight in my car. There is an EV charger. (Submitted by: n, October 2022)

■Report from our website reader: Used on a weekday in September 2022. A small roadside station on the way to the mountains. There is an EV charger. It seems possible to park overnight in a car in the adjacent green space park. However, there was a sign that said "Camping is prohibited." (Submitted by: n, October 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used on a weekday in July 2022. The parking lot is divided into a large vehicle area (west side) and a regular vehicle area (east side), and it was very quiet to rest. The toilets are on the east side. However, as is common at roadside rest areas in mid-summer... the toilets were a mosquito breeding ground. There were also many large flies and small tree frogs. There is an EV fast charger in the corner of the west side parking lot, which can be used for free. (Submitted: August 2022, by n)

■Report from a reader of this site: For better or worse, it's an average roadside rest area as a place to stay overnight in a car. It's somewhat rural, somewhat inconvenient, and somewhat quiet. The adjacent prefectural road has little traffic, but the cars that pass by are without exception speeding, so it's hard to call it tranquil. (Submitted: November 2020, by Y)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used on a weekday in November 2022. This is a new roadside station located on the Okumikawa highway connecting Tono, Nanshin, and Enshu, and it is very popular. The parking lot in front of the main building has limited capacity, but the adjacent sub-parking lot and the second parking lot across the road are spacious enough. EV Quick is available. ■Report from our website reader: Visited on a weekday in November 2022. This is the entrance to Kosaka Onsenkyo, where you can enjoy a rare hot spring with natural, high-concentration carbonated water. It's a small roadside station, but the shop is well-stocked, and you can buy fresh local vegetables at reasonable prices, as well as processed meat and fish products and local Hida sake. The parking lot is in a quiet environment where you can relax. The autumn foliage on the surrounding mountains is wonderful! There is an EV Quick. (Submitted by: n, November 2022)

■Report from our website reader: Designated as a civil engineering heritage site in September 2021. It was once the longest suspension bridge in Japan. Crossing the bridge is free, but the village-run parking lot costs 500 yen. It sways quite a bit, so it might be tough for people with a fear of heights. If you plan to cross it, athletic shoes are recommended. (Submitted by: Ku-kun, October 2021)

■Report from our website reader: Used in January 2021. The parking lot was empty due to the time of year. Traffic on the national highway was light at night, so I was able to sleep peacefully. The toilets are clean and have bidet functions. In the morning, you can see a beautiful sunrise from the coast across the pedestrian crossing, and the World Heritage site, Hanaiwaya Shrine, is right next door, so you can visit in the morning. There is a FamilyMart next door, so shopping is convenient. (Posted by Mr./Ms. I, January 2021)

■Report from our website reader: A new facility that opened in the spring of 2020. It offers specialty products and meals focusing on squid, a local specialty. It also serves as a boarding point for the Tsukumo Bay sightseeing boat. There are few shops in the surrounding area, so it may be necessary to stock up on supplies beforehand. ■Report from our site's readers: Usage fee: Free, not closed at night. Toilets: Not closed at night. Men's toilets are only Japanese-style flush toilet stalls, while the women's/multipurpose toilet has a Western-style flush toilet stall. Both toilets were almost full of toilet paper, and there were several spares, so there's no need to worry. There are sensor-activated lights, so it's safe to use at night, but the men's toilet lights stay on for a short time and there's a sensor at the entrance, so if you need to go to the bathroom at night, it's best to use the multipurpose toilet. Quietness: There are no people around, only the sound of the river and some animal noises. There are no streetlights, so if you get in your car and turn off the interior lights, it becomes completely silent and dark. Other positive points: There are no people around, so there's absolutely nothing to disturb your sleep. Since there is absolutely no light, if your car has a sunroof, you'll probably get a beautiful view of the starry sky. It's very close to Okayama International Circuit, so it's convenient if you want to go there in the morning. Negative points (difficulties): You have to drive down narrow roads to get there (there are no people around, so there's no need to worry about bumping into someone). There is a slight slope (honestly, it doesn't bother me). It's not a popular spot, so security is your own responsibility (though I don't think it will be vandalized). The parking lot is small (I parked next to the toilet, but there was only room for about two cars). The cell phone signal is weak (only 1 out of 4 bars). On a scale of 100, I would rate it... 70 points. Points added: It's quiet because there are no artificial lights, there is a toilet that can be used at night, and it's very close to Okayama International Circuit. Points deducted: The cell phone signal is weak, and you have to drive down narrow roads. Yunogo Onsen, located 20.5km (about 30 minutes) away by car, is recommended as a nearby bathing facility. I especially recommend "Yunogo Sagi Onsenkan" (details). Price: 800 yen per adult (there is a 100 yen discount for JAF members) (Posted: November 2024, by Teitoku)

■Report from our site's reader: The lights go out after 9 PM, but there's no key, so you can still use it. The sensor light inside was working at 5 AM. On weekdays, this parking lot is quiet and there are few other cars, so it was comfortable. The park by the river below the toilet is also free to use. (You can hear the sound of the river roaring.) There is a parking area that can accommodate trailer-type vehicles. (Posted: December 2025, by Catarou)

■Report from our site's reader: On May 24th, it was completely dark and taped up, possibly due to a malfunction. According to Google reviews, the lights are apparently turned off after 9 PM, so it's probably not suitable for overnight stays in a vehicle. (Posted: June 2025, by Osho)

■Report from our site's reader: There is a public toilet. (Posted: September 2020, by 92)

■Report from our site's reader: There are old but clean toilets. It's located along a main road, but traffic is light after sunset and it's quiet at night. There are convenience stores and restaurants nearby. Also, there's the recently opened "Hoshoji Onsen" (details), where the slippery water felt great. You can also eat there. The bathing fee on February 12th was a reasonable 450 yen for adults. However, there's a "Roadside Station Araessa" about 30 minutes away by car, so there might not be much reason to choose this place as accommodation. (Submitted by: Yamabiko, February 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: Currently downgraded to a PA (parking area) and only has vending machines. Because it was formerly a SA (service area), the parking lot is vast, and it's quiet away from the highway. Rather than being quiet, traffic on the Chugoku Expressway has drastically decreased since the completion of the Sanyo Expressway. (Posted: June 2024, Yamabiko)

■Report from our site's reader: Chugoku Expressway, Yoshiwa SA (downbound), used in April 2019. Despite the name "SA," it's the size of a small PA. The gas station is closed. The food court closes at 8 PM. There are few users, both large and small vehicles, making it quite lonely, but it's very quiet. However, music plays continuously in the central vending machine area (though at a low volume), so earplugs might be a good idea. There is an EV fast charger. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our website reader: The originator of Imabari yakitori, where meat is grilled quickly on a griddle without being skewered (details). Tabelog (Posted by: n, May 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a parking lot located along a narrow mountain road that has a surprisingly clean toilet (including a wheelchair-accessible one). It seems to be a parking lot intended for visitors to "Yokono Falls" in the vicinity. The parking space is spacious. There is nothing around, and the road leading there is dangerous (a so-called "rough road"), so it is best to avoid coming here solely for overnight parking. Also, it appears that the toilet is closed during the winter. (Submitted by: C, November 2020)
■Report from our site's reader: A fish restaurant serving set meals. Beware of the huge portions and the owner's personality. (Tabelog)

■Reader Report: An uninhabited island known as the site of the duel between Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojiro. Ferry service available from Shimonoseki Port and Moji Port (details). Details (Submitted by: n, April 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: When I visited after a long time, there were drift marks in the parking lot. Also, there was a sign on the stairs to the observation deck that said, "The small car parking area closes at 6 PM." Neither of these were there when I last visited in 2022. Unfortunately, it may have become a hangout for street racers. Overnight parking is possible in the large car parking area, but there are drift marks there as well. It's not a recommended spot in terms of safety. (Submitted by: y, October 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: This observation deck is famous for its night view of the Seto Ohashi Bridge, so quite a few people come even at night. On the night the poster visited, there were young men and women who liked cars or nightlife until around 11 PM. (Submitted by: y, October 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: It was stated that "there is a very large parking lot, but there are many tire skid marks in the parking lot, and it may be a den of delinquents at night," but the pavement was completely cleaned up a few years ago, and delinquents hardly appear anymore. There are 24-hour restrooms and vending machines, and you can enjoy views of the Seto Ohashi Bridge and the town of Sakaide on the opposite shore. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: A vast multi-purpose park utilizing the riverbed of the Yoshino River. The grounds are so large that it's hard to tell exactly where it is, but there seems to be parking space for about 100 regular cars. There is a toilet on the right side at the bottom of the slope from the embankment road, which is the only access road to this spot. It was newly built in March 2023, is a flush toilet (Western style), and is in good condition. This is an extremely recommended spot for those who want to spend the night in their car in a quiet, secluded place. (Submitted by: y, November 2023)

■Report from our website's readers: If you head north on National Route 491 from the center of Kikugawa town, you will come across a sign for "Osako Meisui" (Osako Famous Water). The road is wide enough for large vehicles to pass through, and you can park in front of the bus stop gazebo. In 1988, when drilling began at a private residence in the area to secure water for daily use, a large amount of groundwater began to gush out from about 20 meters underground. The water temperature was 15 degrees Celsius, it was very tasty, and there was an abundant supply of water that was more than enough for personal use. The current water drawing area was created in 1998 by drawing water from about 100 meters from the source, and a gazebo was also installed. Known as one of the prefecture's leading famous water sources, the area is also known for the "Osako Meisui Festival" held every October, and many people come from far away to draw water.

■Report from a reader of this site: I stopped by for a nap on my way home. It's close to the main road and narrow, so the road noise is quite loud. It's also close to the large vehicle parking area, so it's the worst if there's a truck with its engine running. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: Basic bathing fee 500 yen, additional charges for open-air bath and sauna use. Details: There is a cafeteria inside the reception area. Relaxation room is an additional charge. Located within the grounds of Aeon Mall Hiroshima Gion. (Submitted by: n, February 2024)

■Report from our website reader: There is a great value ticket set that includes Iwakuni Castle, the ropeway, and Kintaikyo Bridge. The ropeway gets very crowded on holidays, so it's best to go to the ropeway parking lot after 8am, purchase your ticket at the counter, and then visit Iwakuni Castle followed by Kintaikyo Bridge.

■Report from a reader of this site: It's like a tourist information center, and they have a footbath during the day. You can park in the parking lot at night too. However, there's a community center and even an elementary school next door, so you need to be careful not to be mistaken for a suspicious person. There are toilets (unknown if they are available at night). (Submitted by: C, November 2020)

■Report from our website reader: Recommended as a stopover for sightseeing. There is a rest area and toilets along the road, but it is unclear whether they are available at night. (Submitted by: h, April 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: Although it is located along a main road, it is on the Sanko Line, so there is little car traffic (no pedestrian traffic even during the evening rush hour) and the number of trains is infrequent. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: It's away from the main road, and the parking lot is spacious, so you can park close to the building and sleep peacefully. (Submitted by: T, August 2025)
■Grand opening on April 20, 2018!

■Report from our website reader: A quiet sports park away from the main road. There is a spacious parking lot north of the baseball field with restrooms. No nighttime closures (older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: The best Kamatama udon in Japan. It's incomparable to a certain touristy udon shop. The best in Japan!

■An extremely popular restaurant. One of the original scenes of Sanuki udon that has now been lost. (Tabelog)

■Report from a reader of this site: The parking lot at Hofu Tenmangu Shrine, which enshrines Sugawara no Michizane, the god of learning. Quiet environment. There are 24-hour restrooms and parking, as well as vending machines and a public telephone. As it is in front of a shrine, please pay your respects at Tenmangu Shrine when using this parking lot. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: I went to this conveyor belt sushi restaurant because I heard they serve local ingredients. It was Saturday night, so there were lots of families, and I sat down thinking it must be a good place. I asked a female waitress for a side dish, and it came out immediately. I took some sushi from the conveyor belt, but I also verbally ordered a recommended dish – a local item. However, it never arrived, even after several minutes. When I inquired, she said, "Just a little longer," and it finally arrived a few minutes later. Then, a little while later, I verbally ordered something else I wanted to eat last, but again, it never came. When I inquired, they acted as if I had just ordered it. In the end, it never arrived, and I left the restaurant. None of the staff seemed to feel any remorse. If they had treated all customers the same way, it might have been acceptable, but other people's orders were arriving one after another. I will never go there again, and I don't want it listed as a recommended restaurant. Sorry for the long post. I had high expectations, so I was extremely disappointed.

■Conveyor belt sushi. If you want to eat local sushi in Sakaiminato, this is the place to go. It's not cheap, but you can eat local sushi at a reasonable price. It's delicious. (Tabelog)

■Report from our site's reader: In the summer, it's a place where young people and families from the neighborhood swim in the sea (or maybe the river?). (If it's your first time, it's probably best not to go after dark. The road is narrow and there's a risk of falling off the road.) There are no toilets, so I don't recommend it, but it might be okay for an overnight stay. There's a public bathhouse, restaurants, and convenience stores nearby.

■Report from a reader of this site: It's cool enough to sleep without air conditioning even in summer, and the second parking lot is really quiet. The toilets are also close, so I recommend it. *Elevation 406m (Posted: August 2025, by t)

■Report from a reader of this site: I used it for the second night of my Golden Week Shikoku tour. If you park in the second parking lot behind the toilets, you can sleep peacefully without being bothered by the noise of traffic. However, at 6am, the song "Amaryllis" is played at high volume from the disaster prevention radio speakers, so it's not suitable for people who want to sleep in late. There is a small Japanese garden behind the building, and you can see the mountains of Kochi Prefecture shrouded in morning mist from the observation deck across the road. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's readers: Temporary toilets available (Submitted by: 92, September 2020)
■Report from our website reader: The restaurant that originated Kudamatsu beef bone ramen. (Reviewed on Tabelog in March 2022 by user n)
■Report from our website reader: Sacred water available at a shrine in Shimonoseki City. Details (Submitted by: n, April 2022)
■Report from a reader of this site: Inside a temple in Shimonoseki City. Parking available. Low water volume. Details (Submitted by: M, October 2022)

■Reader Report: Regarding the Downbound Side. Used on a Sunday in November 2023. It's not a large service area, but there are plenty of spaces for regular cars. The spaces for large vehicles are in a separate block, so I was able to rest without worrying about noise. There is an EV Quick in one corner of the large vehicle space. (Posted by: n, November 2023)
■[Welcome Gate for Local Roads - Upbound Side Only, 24 Hours OK] Spacious and good. The far left is good because trucks don't come there. (Older post from before 2019)

■ Reader Report: There are coin-operated showers 🚿 (24-hour operation, 300 yen/10 minutes) and a coin laundry on the southbound side, but not on the northbound side, so be aware. The freshly baked bread at the bakery located on both sides is delicious and highly recommended. You can sleep well as you are away from the trucks (older post from before 2019).

■ There is free parking for local road users on the southbound side! Available 24 hours a day! Showers are also available! (older post from before 2019)
■Report from our website reader: The restaurant that originated Okayama's famous "Demi-glace Pork Cutlet Rice Bowl". Tabelog, details (Posted: November 2025, by n)

■Report from a reader of this site: Located in the direction of travel from Okayama to Tsuyama. There is a median strip and a public telephone. It is on a slope, but the parking space is quite large. It is also used by a fair number of large vehicles. There is a fair amount of traffic, so measures to reduce noise are necessary. There are no toilets. (Submitted by: C, November 2020)

■Report from our website reader: Although it's a bit far from Okayama city, it's a recommended spot for overnight stays in your car. Only the first parking lot is paid; the second, third, and fourth parking lots are free. There are height restrictions in the first and second parking lots. The third parking lot is close to the terminal but is almost always full. Be prepared to walk from the fourth parking lot. Breakfast is served at the restaurant from 6:15 a.m.

■Report from our website reader: This is a free overnight parking spot I found on my way to Bisei-cho in Okayama Prefecture, which is famous for stargazing. There is a large parking lot, vending machines, and a clean, spacious Western-style toilet. The toilet lights stay on even at night, so you can use it with peace of mind. It is very clean and highly recommended. There is also a restaurant on the premises that sells bento boxes, which are voluminous and delicious 👍 (Posted by: u, July 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: As mentioned in a previous post, the toilets have been renovated and are very clean with showers and heated seats. However, there is only one stall and three urinals in the men's restroom, so it may get crowded and crowded during peak season holidays. On a weekday in May, only a few people were staying overnight in their cars. The ground-level parking lot is not entirely flat, but the second floor of the multi-story parking garage is flat. It is quiet and cool even in summer because it is at an altitude of 1300m. However, there are no convenience stores nearby, so be sure to eat and bathe before staying overnight. (Posted: May 2025, Yamabiko)

■Report from our site's reader: I went to the Tsurugisan lift station parking lot the other day (June 2021), and I wanted to let you know that the dirty toilets have been beautifully renovated. (Posted: July 2021, T)

■Free parking, extremely quiet. Toilets available. Altitude 1359m (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: This is a parking lot near the Hyakken River running course in Asahikawa. There are also places to exercise on the opposite bank of the Hyakken River, and several parking lots there. There are portable toilets in the park. There are no vending machines, but there are some places close to shops. It is close to a main road, but it is not too noisy, so it is ideal for a daytime break. However, it is closed and closed to the public at night, so overnight parking is not possible. (Submitted by: C, October 2020)

■Report from a reader of this site: Parking lot at a sports park located on reclaimed land in the port of Tachibana-cho, Anan City. It's across the Tachibana Bridge from the Tachibana town center. There are two parking lots, but the one closer to the entrance is better (the one closer has a Western-style toilet for disabled people, the one further back doesn't have a Western-style toilet and has a management office, so it's best to avoid it). Parking is free, there are vending machines for drinks, and there are a few streetlights. At night, fishermen occasionally go in and out of the toilets, but otherwise it's quiet. It's close to the Tachibana town center, and supermarkets and convenience stores are about a 3-minute drive away, which is convenient. At night, there were quite a few fishermen on the quay, so it didn't feel like an uninhabited area, but everyone had left by morning. The parking lot is a little distance from the quay, so fishermen come by car to use the toilets, but otherwise there are almost no people coming and going, so you can sleep peacefully. If you are bothered by noise or the presence of people, you should stay a little further away from the toilets. The sports park is surrounded by a fence and locked, and it seemed like it wasn't being used very often. Attached photo (Submitted by: m, September 2021)

■Report from our site's reader: Parking space beyond the passing zone. No median strip. The parking space is narrow and sloped, and there is a risk of rear-end collisions, making it unsuitable as a place to stay overnight in a car. No toilet. (Submitted by: C, November 2020)

■Report from a reader of this site: The main parking lot and other areas are closed at night, but this area is open 24 hours. There are restrooms. Sukiya and McDonald's (both open 24 hours) are within walking distance. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our website reader: A restaurant serving "Chicken Nanban" with an aurora sauce made by mixing mayonnaise and tomato ketchup. Details on Tabelog (Posted by n, July 2025)
■Report from a reader of this site: It's run-down, but it has a toilet, which is good. However, it seems that women wouldn't want to use it. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our website reader: I ate Hotel Matsuo's specialty, the Pirate Bowl (1512 yen including tax). It was impressive and visually appealing, topped with slipper lobster and other ingredients, and it was delicious. The proprietress is friendly, knowledgeable about the local area, and answers questions about the food well. She's beautiful. It's a restaurant on the 7th floor, and there is free parking across the street. Tabelog

■Report from our site's reader: Food court/shops are open from 7:00 to 21:00 on the northbound lane (towards Hiroshima) and from 7:00 to 20:00 on the southbound lane (towards Fukuoka). (Submitted by: n, April 2022)
■There are a lot of trucks and it's noisy. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our website reader: Food court/convenience store open 24 hours (Submitted by: n, February 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: Close to the FamilyMart restroom. Within a 30-minute walk to the arcade. Slightly less noisy from trains than AtPark JR Matsuyama Station. 500 yen/24 hours. (Submitted by: m, October 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: A very vast riverside spot. It's not an official campsite, but it's a place where you can pitch tents, have BBQs, and try canoeing. There are campers all year round. There are no sinks or water sources. The toilets are portable toilets, but they are simple Western-style toilets, so they don't smell and are perfectly usable. Toilet paper is also replenished. The area is very large, so you can maintain a reasonable distance from your neighbors. However, since it's free, some troublemakers may come. Leaving charcoal unattended, making loud noises until late at night, idling engines, etc. Depending on the season, the number of troublemakers may increase, so be careful. If it's sunny, the sun shines from early in the morning, so it's perfect for solar charging portable power supplies. Since it's a riverside, it can be windy on some days. For shopping, there's a Lawson convenience store nearby, and if you go a little further, there's a discount supermarket called Dio, and various other options. Personally, I like this place. (Submitted by: m, February 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: There are toilets, parking spaces, and neither the toilets nor the restrooms are closed at night. There are people fishing and camping, but it is quiet at night. Since there are houses nearby, be mindful of your manners. The view from the sandy beach is nice, and you can enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of the Seto Inland Sea. (Submitted by k, February 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: I only used the toilet and didn't stay overnight, but it seems like it would be possible to park here overnight. Usage fee: Free. It doesn't seem to be closed at night. There is a flush toilet (no bidet) and it is very clean. It is quiet despite being next to a main road, as there is not much traffic. You could get a good night's sleep if you park further back. It is 50m from the sea. The elevation is 3.7m above sea level. (Posted by naka0514k in December 2023)

■ Reader Report: The toilets are locked outside of the facility's operating hours. There are no toilets in the surrounding area. (Submitted by: Ninja, August 2025)
■ Reader Report: The toilets are very clean and available 24 hours a day, right next to the Kyushu-Shikoku Ferry Terminal. The facility's parking lot is small, so I don't think it's possible for a campervan. It might be possible in the corner of the ferry terminal's parking lot. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a sign in the restroom asking people to refrain from staying overnight in their vehicles. It seems the facility does not welcome overnight stays in vehicles. I ended up staying overnight without noticing, but as a parking spot, it's a normal roadside station. The adjacent Route 425 has relatively little traffic at night, so I was able to spend a fairly quiet night. (Submitted by: y, October 2023)
■Report from a reader of this site: The restrooms are now closed from 10 PM to 5 AM. The supermarket remains open 24 hours. (Confirmed November 2017)

■Report from our site's reader: There is a restroom. If you park in the rightmost spot in front of the restroom, you can see the Kurushima Kaikyo Bridge from inside your car. In addition to the observation deck, there is also an observation deck a minute or two down the road, where you can buy local snacks at Saisaikiteya (in Imabari city) or the roadside station and enjoy a beer while watching the Kurushima Kaikyo Bridge at sunset. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There are toilets and vending machines. In the past, there was nothing but toilets, so it was easy to use, but now that there are shops, it might be better to refrain from using it for long periods of time (overnight stays in your car). (Submitted by: C, November 2020)

■Report from a reader of this site: A facility with only toilets and vending machines. It is adjacent to a smart interchange (24-hour operation). The rest area cannot be used when exiting from the smart interchange on either the inbound or outbound lanes (the rest area can be used when entering from the smart interchange). (Submitted by: n, May 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: This park is located on the shore of Lake Ikeda, a dam lake, and has parking space for about 50-100 regular cars. The toilets are located about 50m north of the parking area and are flush toilets, including Western-style ones. The Tokushima Expressway runs directly above, but surprisingly, the noise from passing cars is not that noticeable. *Toilet location 👉️Details (Posted: November 2023, by y)

■Report from our site's reader: There are two parking lots, one above and one below the dam. There are no toilets at either location. The parking lot above the dam is in front of the management office, and the road leading up to it is a little narrow. There is a small park in front of the parking lot below the dam. There are benches with roofs. However, there is also a sign warning of venomous snakes. It is along a national highway, but there is hardly any traffic and it is quiet. It is quite far from houses, shops, and convenience stores. (Posted: December 2020)

■Report from our site's reader: A parking lot frequented by surfers. Toilets available, but no running water. The parking lot is small, so during the autumn and winter surfing season, you'll almost certainly need to park at night to find a spot. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from our site's reader: A parking lot frequented by surfers. Toilets available, but no running water. There's a delicious restaurant nearby run by surfers. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: There is a Lawson convenience store a few minutes' drive to the west. There is an A-Coop supermarket in front of the station, but be aware that it closes early at 7:00 PM. There is some traffic as a national highway runs nearby, but it is not bothersome. (Older post from before 2019)
■Report from a reader of this site: There's a convenience store, open from 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM. You can buy bento boxes and beer. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: Comment: Occasionally, you'll see people night fishing in the free parking lot. For fishing enthusiasts, it might be nice to camp in your car and fish 🎣. Whether you'll actually catch anything is unknown 🙏 There are toilets in the park. They're the typical park toilets, but they're cleaned and kept in good condition. There's a road right in front, but the noise wasn't noticeable. It's relatively quiet. There were people walking around from the morning, so it seems to be a popular park. There's also a famous supermarket nearby called Nikenya Shoten. It's a supermarket, but it has days off. Please be careful. (Posted by: Katakata, July 2025)

■Report from a reader of this site: I stayed here in May of this year based on the information here, but it was terrible. It was a hangout for delinquents at night. Motorcycles and modified cars were using it as a base, coming and going with loud noises, making it impossible to sleep. Even on weekday nights, it was no good. If you're staying nearby, I recommend the free "Ijiri Parking Lot" (details) under the Usa Bridge. There are 24-hour toilets. I ended up moving there instead. (Older post from before 2019)

■Free parking along the coast. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from our site's reader: There are two coin-operated showers at the laundromat (open 24 hours) - 300 yen/8 minutes - shampoo, soap, and hair dryer available (Submitted by: Camp Oyaji, June 2025)

■Report from our site's reader: There are clean public restrooms. There are a few cars with couples in them, but it's like having the place to yourself late at night. More comfortable than a roadside station. For a bath, there's "Taki Ichijiku Onsen" 2km away. However, there's a sign prohibiting fireworks, so you need to be careful of young people on summer nights. (Submitted by Takenii in July 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: There is a fairly large parking lot, and several parking lots nearby that are exclusively for the ski season. During the ski season, it is a parking lot for skiers, but during the off-season, it is a parking lot for hikers. The relatively clean toilets (Japanese style) in the campground's administration building were usable even late at night. The lights turn on automatically. The administration building is closed and unusable during the ski season. There is only a vending machine for drinks, but I think it is the highest elevation parking lot in Hiroshima Prefecture. It is usable if your purpose is hiking. The nearest convenience store is more than 20 kilometers away. (Submitted by: h, August 2022)

■Report from a reader of this site: This parking space is located on a slope in the middle of a curve. There is no median strip. It is dangerous if cars try to take a shortcut, so it is best to avoid it as a place to park overnight, but large vehicles are sometimes parked there. (Submitted by: C, November 2020)

■Report from a reader of this site: Address for car navigation search: 3061 Hijiki, Yanai City, Yamaguchi Prefecture. Take a short detour off National Route 437. Details (Submitted by: Mr./Ms. N, November 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: This is a delicious pizza place!! Definitely check it out!! The portions are generous! However, be careful as the parking lot is small. Closed on Tuesdays.

■The weekday lunch pizza is a great deal and highly recommended. (Tabelog)

■Report from our site's reader: It's located in a corner of the parking lot of Aeon Mall Hiyoshizu. Inside, there's Yamayoshitei, famous for its seafood bowls, as well as a fish shop, a butcher shop, and a tempura shop. The fish shop sells fresh fish from Sakaiminato, Tottori Prefecture (rock oysters and tuna in summer, snow crab in winter) at about 20% cheaper than the fish market and seafood processing center in Sakaiminato, due to its location in the parking lot of a huge supermarket. Also, since it closes at 5pm, they offer prepared foods such as sushi, grilled fish, and fried fish at half price from early in the day. (Submitted by Yamabiko, June 2024)
■Report from our website reader: 900 yen, details available. There is a cafeteria and rest area inside the reception area. (Submitted by: n, February 2024)
■Report from our website reader: 900 yen, details. The food was delicious. It's close to Miyajima, so it might be good before sleeping in your car. (Submitted by: h, May 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: The entrance fee is 400 yen between 8:30 and 18:00, but entry is free between 18:00 and 22:30. The gate closes between 22:30 and 6:00, so you can take a walk around Katsurahama or just go to sleep. Since payment is made in advance, once you're inside, it's free. There are several clean toilets with automatic lighting throughout the park. There's also one near the parking lot. If you stay near the tourist information center, you can use Wi-Fi, although it's weak. I stayed there around February, and it was nice because it was dark and quiet. (Posted by: k, February 2023)
■Report from our website reader: 700 yen, details: Cafeteria (ticket system). (Submitted by: n, June 2024)

■Report from our site's reader: 620 yen, facility's website. This is an accommodation facility, but I used it for a day trip to the baths. The men's and women's baths alternated every day. There is also an open-air bath. It was crowded, probably because it was a busy time, but it was a great help as there were no other bathing facilities nearby. (Submitted by: A, October 2024)
■Report from a reader of this site: There is parking for about 5 cars, but there is a toilet. It is directly under the Seto Ohashi Bridge, so there may be some noise. (Older post from before 2019)

■Report from a reader of this site: Used on February 13th. The front parking lot had more space for large vehicles than when I used it before, but the entry and exit routes for large and small vehicles were separated by poles. The parking lot at the back with the EV charging facilities was dark and quiet as there were no streetlights. Also, there were small signs on the sinks in the toilets that said, "Please refrain from using the roadside station for overnight stays" and "Please do not pour ramen broth down the drain." (Submitted by Yamabiko, February 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: It's located along National Route 9, and there are also truck parking spaces, so it's a bit noisy. It's very spacious, but at night all the parking spaces were filled with vehicles parked overnight. The parking space at the back is quiet, but there is a sign that says, "Please refrain from taking breaks at night for security reasons." ■Report from a reader of this site: I would like to report on the car camping spot where I actually stayed overnight in Nagasaki City on June 6, 2024. Rates: Maximum 400 yen from 9 PM to 8 AM the next morning, maximum 1400 yen from 8 AM to 9 PM (only the furthest sections 5, 6, 7, and 8), 100 yen for every 20 minutes at all times. It is a small parking lot with about 12 spaces, but there were no other cars when I stayed there. The public toilets at Dejima Wharf (clean flush toilets) are just across the road (a few steps away) and are available 24 hours a day. There was little traffic on the adjacent road at night, so I was able to sleep well. It is a parking lot adjacent to the well-located Dejima Wharf, so you can enjoy meals on the terrace or take a walk. Glover Garden, Meganebashi Bridge, Shianbashi Bridge, Chinatown, Confucius Temple, and Hamamachi are all within walking distance, so it is also recommended as a base for sightseeing in Nagasaki. The toilets are a bit small but clean. There are convenience stores and supermarkets within a 10-minute drive. I think it's a good base for sightseeing around Ibusuki and Mount Kaimon. The parking lot is paved up to the railway tracks to the north, but be careful if you park near the tracks as the roar of the railway bridge can be heard late at night. There is also a highway running in front of the tracks, but the traffic noise at night is not that bothersome. For shopping, there is a convenience store in 3 minutes by car. If you go to the city, there are supermarkets and Don Quijote and everything you need. As of December 30, 2022, there are still many campers. There are also a few people sleeping in their cars. Here, there are public restrooms and vending machines between the parking lot and the sports field. ■Report from our site's readers: A vast riverside park. Note that it is not a campsite. It is merely a "park" where you are permitted to pitch tents, so please do not misunderstand. However, it is a very popular spot, and even in this cold season, there are a considerable number of tents and many cars where people are sleeping in. I myself have been staying there for several days now, sleeping in my car. Since it is not a campsite, there is no water source. And there is only one toilet, so depending on where you park your car, the toilet may be very far away. The toilet has a heated seat with a bidet. And perhaps thanks to the kindness of the locals, there are many amenities provided (toothpaste, hand warmers, dish soap, etc.). It also seems to be a popular spot for moles, as there are molehills everywhere. Be careful not to get poked from below by moles when you pitch your tent (lol). For shopping, there are supermarkets, 100-yen shops, drugstores, home centers, convenience stores, etc. all within a 5-minute drive, which is very convenient. At the Marushoku Mifune supermarket, prepared foods are half price around 4 pm. And they are delicious. It's pitch black at night, and the stars are beautiful. Personally, I highly recommend this place. (Posted by: M, December 2022)

■Report from our site's reader: There are several parking spaces next to the public toilets. To be honest, it's such a rural area that nobody really complains even if you park on the side of the road, but since it's a single road with no detours, please leave enough space for other cars to pass. Local campers occasionally have BBQs there. / The paved open space facing the sea near the park isn't a free parking lot, but it's not private property and is a port work area, so you can park there for extended periods. It is surprisingly easy to access as it is very close to the Itoda roadside station on Route 201. If you go at night, it is easy to miss the sign for the road leading up to the parking lot. ■Report from our site's reader: Restrooms available. This is a parking lot for tourists visiting "Ogyu Falls," which is featured in an Amazon commercial (details). It's quite rural, so it's practically deserted, and there are no designated parking spaces, giving you a lot of freedom. It's pitch black and a bit scary at night, but on the other hand, the stars are beautiful. There's Miyagi Onsen nearby, but Shiratani Onsen, 6km to the west, is more recommended for bathing. (Submitted by Takenii, January 2023)

■Report from our site's reader: No toilets, no vending machines, "no electricity." This is the site of a former Catholic settlement of hidden Christians, which has been uninhabited for over 10 years. The road to get there is extremely technical, barely wide enough for a small car, impossible to pass, no guardrails, bumpy concrete road, prone to falling rocks, a continuous steep mountain pass, and a risk of slipping and falling if a wheel comes off, and it takes about an hour each way to reach it, but it is treated like a free natural campsite. The wooden houses and stone walls in the settlement are at extremely high risk of collapse, so it is best not to get close. Although land access is difficult, it is easy by sea, so some people land from the eastern breakwater side. (Submitted by: m, June 2024)

Note 1) It is easy to mistake this for a private property, but the gravel vacant lot adjacent to the park is privately owned (there used to be a house there). The park parking lot is the long, narrow paved area next to the sidewalk at the back. Note 2) Heisei Elementary School across the road is closed, but it is leased to the manager of a privately run direct sales store, so if you enter the premises without permission during unmanned hours such as at night, an alarm will sound (silently) and mobile patrol officers or the police will come. ■Report from our site's reader: There are countless other places nearby where you can park for extended periods. Because it is part of a project to revitalize a depopulated village, in addition to the nearby tourist attraction, a Catholic church, there are also private salt factories repurposed from abandoned old houses, hotels converted from abandoned schools, and guesthouses in old houses, so it is surprisingly crowded. There used to be a public toilet and water intake facility on the site of the abandoned school that could be used 24 hours a day, but the management has changed and the building has been renovated, so you need to check whether it is still usable. Similar to the Okuno-Mafushi settlement, the road leading here is narrow, unlit, and full of loose rocks, requiring a continuous steep uphill drive of about 30 minutes each way, so it is not recommended unless you are very confident in your driving skills. If you drive your car off the road, you will probably die (seriously). (Submitted by: m, June 2024)

■Report from a reader of this site: A quiet parking lot at night, despite being within walking distance of the downtown area. Public toilets in the park across the street are available 24 hours a day. There are many streetlights leading to the toilets, so a flashlight is not necessary. Three parking lots are adjacent to each other, but all have different pricing systems. This parking lot has a night-time maximum of 800 yen from 6 PM to 8 AM the next day, and a daytime maximum of 1000 yen at 100 yen for 30 minutes. However, vehicles over 2.5m in height are charged the large vehicle rate, so campervans should be careful. The north side parking lot does not have a night-time rate and is more expensive. The Water Garden parking lot on the other side of the road is noisy with skateboarders, as mentioned in that report. There are several cars parked overnight, and there have been no police questioning or anything like that, so there are no concerns about safety. I often use this place because I can have a drink in Shianbashi and then sleep there cheaply. (Posted by f, December 2023)

■Report from a reader of this site: A personal hidden gem. It is a lively free barbecue spot during the day, but at night there are hardly any cars and it is very quiet. Idling is strictly prohibited as there are houses nearby. The toilets are flush toilets and clean, but there are no lights, so a flashlight or lantern is necessary at night. The view overlooking the dam is superb, and drinking coffee while enjoying the view in the park in the open area first thing in the morning is a blissful moment. The hot spring is Oasis Sasaguri at the foot of the mountain; it is an artificial hot spring, but the water quality is good and it is cheap at 330 yen. (Posted by: Ms. A, December 2020)

■【No Entry】Highly praised by hot spring enthusiasts. This hot spring is considered the Yokozuna (grand champion) of wild hot springs in Western Japan. I, the administrator, have also visited. I have marked its exact location on this map, so please use it as a reference.

■Administrator's Rating ★5 (Spring Quality 4.5, Scenery 0.5) Simply amazing. Absolutely incredible. The title of "Strongest Wild Hot Spring" is well-deserved. First, the spring water is a bluish acidic spring, and the hot spring water mixes with the river water to create a slightly hot, just-right temperature. This is miraculous. It's superb, nothing more to say. And the scenery is also spectacular, offering a panoramic view of hell. On the other side of the river, sulfurous steam is forcefully spewing out of a hole. A miracle of nature is manifested here. I, the administrator, couldn't help but put my hands together in prayer. Truly a sanctuary of hot springs. A perfect score of感動 (deep emotion). By the way, insects are present, so bringing insect repellent is recommended.
